title: Fix silent fallback to dummy results in results_parser.py
description: results_parser.py falls back to dummy/fabricated result data when FRD parsing fails, with no error raised and no warning surfaced to the engineer. An engineer can receive a plausible-looking displacement/stress result that is completely made up. This must raise ResultProcessingError instead of silently returning fake data.
close_reason: Closed

title: Elastic supports (numeric stiffness) are analysed as free, silently
description: A support condition with a numeric stiffness below 1e12 (IfcLinearStiffnessMeasure etc.) is treated as free by _local_fixity(), with no warning: a spring under a column or a partially fixed base is left out, which breaks aiz.12. Measured 2026-10-17 by hand on CalculiX 2.23: SPRING1 in DOF 1-3 on an expanded B32R node and on S6 nodes works (tip deflection P/(kb+k) to 4 figures; plate on equal springs settles F/k exactly). SPRING1 in DOF 4-6 on a beam node is accepted and does nothing. A stiff B31 arm with a translational SPRING1 at its tip (k_t = k_r/a^2) gives the rotational spring to 0.04%. RF does not include the spring force: the reaction is k u. Plan: springs for point and line supports (per length: tributary length of each node), translations as SPRING1 (global axis) or SPRINGA to a fixed helper node (skew), rotations through an arm on nodes of curve members; on shell-only nodes raise until the drilling freedom is dealt with. Reactions add k u.
notes: 2026-10-17 done: support_springs() / _build_support_springs(): each spring a SPRING1 on a node of its own tied by an *EQUATION to what it resists (translation, or an arm's rotation); reactions k u from SPRING_NODES printed each step; HRZ shares along edges and over faces; units by power of length in get_connection_input(). Measured through the pipeline: beam_01 on a pin and a 1e6 N/m spring settles P/2k to 1e-3, rotational spring end moment 8533.7 against 8529 by hand (0.05%, shear left out), the solver's forces kept and the diagram's end moment agreeing to 1e-5; slab edges on vertical and rotational springs per metre give the strip's end moments to 0.05%. Tests: TestElasticSupports, TestSurfaceSupports.test_slab_edges_on_springs.
close_reason: Closed

title: building_01: four beams lose their end element to an overlapping beam and are not joined to their columns
description: Found 2026-10-13 while checking how eccentric member ends are joined. building_01.ifc has beams 29 and 42 (x = 8 m, y 2.225 to 5.775, at z = 6 and 3 m) lying wholly inside beams 6 and 2. They get no physical group elements, so MeshMapper._map_by_spatial_fallback(allow_sharing=True) gives them every beam element whose centroid is within 0.6 x their length (2.13 m) of their own centroid: a ball, not a line. After the writer takes away what earlier members own, each keeps 2 elements, which are the last elements (x 7.33 to 7.775) of the beams that frame in at right angles: 31 and 63 at z = 6, 43 and 59 at z = 3. Those four beams then have no mesh node at their end (nearest 0.44 m away), and 29 and 42 have none at theirs (0.318 m), so _find_connection_nodes_at_location() returns nothing for either at connections 22, 25, 32 and 33, and _merge_rigid_connection_nodes() writes no rigid link: 8 of the file's 48 IfcRelConnectsWithEccentricity ends are not joined (41 links: 16 column tops, 24 beam ends, 1 other). The beams are held by the slab line ties only, and their end elements have the section of 29/42. No warning says a connection was not made; the overlap warning lists 43 and 59 as overlapping, which they are not. building_02 is not affected (640 curve members, all with a node at both ends at a 2 m mesh). Reproduce: scratch script that prints, before _merge_rigid_connection_nodes, each curve member's nearest own node to each of its ends (mesh size 0.5).
acceptance_criteria: An overlapped curve member is given only elements lying on its own line (or none); every member of a connection either gets a node there or the analysis stops or warns naming the member and connection; building_01 has a rigid link for all 48 eccentric ends, with a test.
close_reason: Physical groups are now made per set of owning members (gmsh_geometry._create_physical_groups), so a member overlapping another over a part shares a group named A||B for that part. MeshMapper's proximity fallback is removed: a member with no elements in the mesh raises MeshingError. The writer keeps _geometry_element_sets so an overlapped member with no elements of its own is still found at its connections, and _check_members_reach_their_connections() raises when a curve member has no node at a connection. building_01 has a rigid link for all 48 eccentric ends (was 40), reactions unchanged (282.0 / 13.5 kN). Tests: TestBuilding01Joints, two in test_physical_group_mapping.py with real Gmsh, TestMembersReachTheirConnections. Full suite 1276 passed on the local ccx 2.23; not run against the 2.21 shim. Not committed.

title: portal_01 analysed with twice its load: the locations of a curve action's values were not read
description: Found working on aiz.58. portal_01's IfcStructuralCurveAction (LINEAR) has an IfcStructuralLoadConfiguration with two equal values of 100 lbf/in at Locations 96 and 192 in along its 192 in beam: a load on the right half. LoadsExtractor ignored Locations and applied it over the whole member with no warning: 19 200 lbf (85.4 kN) shared equally by the feet, for the 9600 lbf (42.7 kN) the file states; a load with differing values was applied at its mean over the whole member with a warning. Also not read: ProjectedOrTrue (a load per projected length was applied per true length), and a curve action's PredefinedType (SINUS/PARABOLA applied as a constant load of the peak; a single force on a curve action, DISCRETE, applied as that many N/m). extract_all_loads listed every linear action twice (unused by the pipeline). Fixed 2026-10-12: LineLoad.samples, _varying_line_load_to_nodal_forces, _seed_load_points, _per_true_length; the unsupported kinds raise ModelExtractionError. portal_01's vertical reactions now match the results stored in its own file to 0.02%; thrust is 1.9% lower because that program used a shear area of 0.79 A and we use the web (a plane frame with the web's shear area agrees with ours to 0.7%). Tests: TestPortalAgainstTheResultsInItsFile, TestLoadThatVariesAlongABeam, TestLoadsAlongAMember, TestLoadThatVariesAlongItsMember.
close_reason: Fixed 2026-10-12 with aiz.58 part 3; see description.

title: SelfWeightCoefficients of a load case is not applied
description: IfcStructuralLoadCase.SelfWeightCoefficients gives the share of the members' weight a case includes along global x, y, z. Dead has (0,0,-1) in beam_01, building_01 and building_02. It is now read (LoadGroup.self_weight_coefficients) and a warning says it is not applied, but the case and every combination including it are without self-weight; in building_02 Dead has nothing else, so it has no step and '1.4D' is only 1.4 Extra_dead. Fix: write *DLOAD GRAV scaled by the coefficients in that case's step (the step load recorder already handles GRAV for reactions; U1 models need the lumped CLOAD path), give a case with coefficients a step even when it has no actions, and decide what --gravity then means (separate Gravity case as now, or only for models whose cases have no coefficients). Blast radius: Dead results of the three example models, most beam_01 benchmarks (they assume 20 kN only), README/validation tables. Needs Bruno's decision on --gravity semantics.
close_reason: A load case's step now has the members' weight scaled and turned by SelfWeightCoefficients (g = 9.81); a case with nothing else is a case; --gravity stays a separate Gravity case for files with no load case and warns when the file already has self-weight. beam_01 weight alone: 8829.0 N, wL2/12 to 0.1%, deflection 1.2%. building_02 1.4D+1.6L 226.18 MN, 54.4 mm (was 132.4 MN, 44.5 mm).

title: CI red since 2026-10-11: CalculiX 2.21 misreports reactions at supports that hold a rotation
description: CI installs calculix-ccx 2.21 (Ubuntu 24.04); development is on 2.23. Same input, same displacements, different RF at a node whose rotations are restrained: clamped bar 1076.6 for 1000 N; portal_01 feet 34165 and 44124 for 42703 each; beam_01 end resultant 11390 for 10000 (errors cancel in the total); balcony frame root 444 for 1000. In the FRD one expanded node of the clamped face lacks one force component. Three benchmark tests of reaction totals failed on CI from the commit that added them (column-slab ties, placed models); nothing before them tested a reaction at a clamped support along the member. Reproduced with a podman image of ubuntu:24.04 + calculix-ccx and a ccx shim in PATH.
close_reason: ResultsExporter checks each rotation-holding support against its member end forces (3%) and each load case against its applied load (0.1%); replaces with member end forces where it can, marks the rest unreliable, and plausibility.balance_warnings() says so. Tests of the solver's own reactions at clamped supports skip on 2.21 (_needs_solver_reactions); TestSolverReactionsAreChecked runs on both. Whole fast suite passes against 2.21 locally. Follow-ups: 94g children.

title: Reactions left out loads applied at support nodes, and counted loads in a support's free directions
description: CalculiX RF is the force inside the structure at a node, not the reaction. Measured 2026-10-11 on a 2 m beam: 100 N on a node in a held direction reads 0 there; 70 N in a free direction of a roller reads 70 N. Every reaction total under a distributed load or self-weight was short by the share on the support nodes (cantilever_01 17.34 of 18.36 N at 1 m; slab_01 219.7 of 229.6 N; the 2.5 kPa plate 34.8 of 37.5 kN), and a point load on a support was missing altogether.
close_reason: Fixed with 94g.1: write_analysis_steps records the loads on support nodes (_StepLoadRecorder, _weight_on_nodes) and ResultsExporter takes them off. Reactions equal the applied loads at any mesh; tolerances in the benchmarks tightened from 2% to 0.01%.

title: CalculixRunner could solve a different input file from the one written
description: It ran model.inp instead of analysis.inp when one five times larger lay in the working directory, did not replace an analysis.inp left by an earlier run in the output directory, inserted a *HEADING into large inputs, edited and reran after 'increase ne_' errors, and collected result files of any name when its own were missing. Now: the given input, as written, once, and only its own result files. Tests: tests/unit/analysis/test_correct_inp.py.
close_reason: Found and fixed with aiz.59

title: Supports were invented or silently dropped by the support writer
description: write_boundary_conditions fixed every node at y = 0 when a model had no support (BC_AUTO), left out a support with no mesh node within 0.1 m, moved a line support with no node on its edge to its midpoint, and get_constrained_dofs fixed all six DOF of a 'rigid' connection holding one member even without a support condition. Not exception handlers, so the aiz.12 audit missed them. None fired on the example models; about 25 tests relied on them. Now AnalysisError / nothing restrained. Tests: tests/unit/analysis/test_supports_are_never_made_up.py.
close_reason: Found and fixed with aiz.59

title: Members and supports were dropped or given defaults when extraction failed
description: Found in aiz.12. A member whose extraction raised was left out and the analysis ran without it; no material or profile gave steel and a 0.1 x 0.2 m section; no thickness gave 0.1 m; a material with no Young's modulus was 210 GPa and with no density 7850 kg/m3; a connection with no position went to the origin; a surface connection became a point support; a curve connection with no edge became a point support; PlacementRelTo was ignored with an info log; Extractor.warnings never reached result['warnings']. A second extractor (PropertiesExtractor) only ever ran on slabs and gave each a default section. All now raise ModelExtractionError naming the entity, or warn in the results (no density: weightless; no Poisson ratio: 0.3). PropertiesExtractor, ifc/geometry/, gmsh_utils.py and utils/validation.py (never imported by the pipeline) deleted.
close_reason: Fixed in the aiz.12 round, with tests

title: Loads were made up when they could not be applied: node 2, 1 kN, first member of the model
description: Found in aiz.12. boundary_condition_handling: a point load with no position went to node 2 (default_node); a force vector that could not be read became [0,-1000,0]; a distributed load naming no member was put on the first curve/surface member; magnitude defaulted to 1000. LoadsExtractor: a point load with no position went to the origin, an area load with no member to 'default_surface' (which then hit an AttributeError on self.ifc_file that a broad handler hid), an unsupported applied load became a zero force, applied moments were dropped, and a mock IFC object triggered a path returning invented test loads. All now raise AnalysisError/ModelExtractionError naming the load. Tests: tests/unit/analysis/test_loads_are_never_made_up.py, tests/unit/ifc/test_extraction_fails_loudly.py.
close_reason: Fixed in the aiz.12 round, with tests

title: Beam on two ball supports spins about its own axis; deflection reported twice too large
description: Found by the pinned-support benchmark (aiz.20). Supports fixing dx, dy, dz and no rotation at both ends leave a beam free to rotate about its axis. CalculiX solves anyway with an arbitrary rotation; displacements are read on the faces of the expanded section, so beam_01 reported 2.92 mm instead of 1.34 mm, with no warning. Fix: UnifiedCalculixWriter._hold_spinning_members() finds curve members with no torsional restraint (no support fixing rotation about the axis, no joint to another member without a torsional release) and restrains that rotation at one support, with a warning; members along a skew axis or without a support of their own are reported only.
close_reason: Fixed; unit tests and TestSimplySupportedBeam.

title: Channels read from a non-existent IFC entity; unsupported profiles analysed as a default rectangle
description: Found by the T/L/C benchmarks (aiz.20). Both extractors tested is_a('IfcChannelProfileDef'), which is not an IFC entity; a real channel (IfcUShapeProfileDef) fell through to the default 0.1 x 0.2 m rectangle with a log line only (682% out on a cantilever). Any unsupported profile did the same. Fix: channels read from IfcUShapeProfileDef; an unsupported profile raises ModelExtractionError naming member and profile, and the extractor no longer swallows it. Note: other member-extraction failures are still collected as extractor warnings and the member dropped (see aiz.12).
close_reason: Fixed; unit tests with real IFC entities and channel benchmarks.

title: Hollow profiles read as solid, solid circles as a default rectangle; CalculiX PIPE section wrong
description: Found while checking 31a's note on PIPE/BOX. (1) IfcCircleHollowProfileDef and IfcRectangleHollowProfileDef are subtypes of the solid profiles, and both extractors tested is_a() on the solid type first, so every box was a solid rectangle. (2) IfcCircleProfileDef had no handler and fell back to a default 0.1 x 0.2 rectangle. (3) CalculiX SECTION=PIPE on B32R gave a cantilever 83% too flexible with the weight of a solid bar; B31 rejects PIPE. Cantilever errors before: bar 68%, tube 83%, box 54%. Fix: hollow types tested first and built with Section.create_hollow_*; circle handler added; hollow circular shear area by Cowper; only RECT is written natively, everything else goes through the equivalent rectangle. All three now 0.2% from beam theory (TestRoundAndHollowSections).
close_reason: Fixed with 31a; unit tests with real IFC entities and three pipeline benchmarks.

title: Slabs connected only at their corners span corner to corner; beams under their edges carry nothing
description: building_02 connects every slab at its four corner point connections only. 576 curve members lie along slab edges or in walls with no connection between the corners. Beam and shell meshes have separate nodes and are joined only at connections, so the 8.5 x 21.4 m ground slab under 16 kPa Live spanned from corner to corner (462 mm) while the edge beam beside it moved 0.1 mm. Fix: UnifiedCalculixWriter._build_line_bearings() ties every node of a curve member lying in a surface member to the shell element it falls in (DOF 1-3, shell shape functions), written last by _write_line_bearings(). One warning reports the count. building_02 at 2 m: Live 462 -> 25.8 mm, Extra_dead 42 -> 15.3, self-weight 120 -> 16.8; reactions unchanged; 4 m vs 2 m now 7%. Benchmark: slab on two cantilever beams (edges and inset), 0.5% and 0.1% from the cantilever formula.
close_reason: Fixed: line bearings in the writer, 17 unit tests and a Tier 2 benchmark.

title: Distributed loads were written by magnitude only, along element axes
description: Line loads were written as '*DLOAD <set>, P2, |q|' and area loads as '*DLOAD <set>, P, |p|': a pressure along the beam's local 2 axis, or normal to the shell, with the sign and direction of the IFC load discarded (and a magnitude of 1000 substituted when it was not positive). On building_02 the 480 vertical line loads of Extra_dead pushed floor beams sideways (333 mm horizontal), and the total reaction had the wrong sign. Fixed: _distributed_load_to_nodal_forces() computes work-equivalent nodal forces in global axes for B31/B32R/S3/S6/S4/S8 and they are written as *CLOAD; IFC GlobalOrLocal is read and local loads rotated with the member axes. building_02 applied loads by hand: Live 30.017 MN, Extra_dead 60.286 MN; reactions 30.017 and 60.283 MN. Not handled: PROJECTED_LENGTH, loads over part of a member, linearly varying loads (averaged).
close_reason: Fixed while working on aiz.29; unit tests in test_distributed_loads.py and line-load benchmarks in two directions.

title: Joints along a member's span were attached to the member's nearest end
description: _find_connection_nodes_at_location() targeted whichever end of a curve member was nearest the connection. A secondary beam framing into the span of a main beam (grid_of_beams: joints at x = 0 and +-1.45 on a main beam running from -3 to 3) was therefore tied to the main beam's end node, next to the support, up to 3 m away; and no mesh node existed at the joint anyway, because _seed_support_points() only seeded supports. Fixed: every connection position lying inside a curve member is seeded, and the target is the point of the member nearest the connection (projection onto its axis), falling back to the nearest end when no node is there. Found while working on aiz.30.
close_reason: Fixed with aiz.30; tests in test_topology_node_finding.py, test_support_point_seeding.py and the grid_of_beams benchmark.

title: Rigid-linked joint was also tied in translation, clamping the joint
description: A member that stops short of its joint (column ending at the slab soffit) is bridged by a stiff B31 link in _merge_rigid_connection_nodes(). _write_point_connection() then also wrote *EQUATION on DOF 1-3 between the two ends of that link. Two points 0.15 m apart that are rigidly linked and have equal translations cannot rotate, so the slab was clamped at the column: structure_01 slab deflection 0.33 mm on the Column_02 side against 0.40 in the reference. Fixed: nodes joined by a rigid link get no equations (_rigid_link_groups). Found while working on aiz.26.
close_reason: Fixed in the same round as aiz.26; regression tests added.

title: Support conditions were written in global axes; IFC gives them in the connection's own axes
description: IfcBoundaryNodeCondition / IfcBoundaryEdgeCondition are expressed in the connection's local axes: ConditionCoordinateSystem for a point connection, and for a curve connection x along the edge with Axis giving local z. get_constrained_dofs() mapped dx..drz straight to global DOF 1-6. structure_01's wall base (edge along global Y, T,T,T,T,F,F) was held about global X (drilling) instead of about its own edge, so the wall leant over: 0.28-0.42 mm of sway against 0.07 mm in the Code_Aster reference, growing with mesh refinement. Fixed: connections carry local_axes (ConnectionsExtractor._extract_local_axes) and get_constrained_dofs() permutes the flags into global DOFs when the axes are parallel to the global ones. Found while working on aiz.26.
close_reason: Fixed in the same round as aiz.26; regression tests added.

title: results.json per-member displacements: missing for curve members, wrong for surfaces on building_02
description: In a structure_01 run the two column entries in results.json had no 'envelope'/max displacement while both surface members did. Beam results come back on CalculiX's expanded nodes; confirm node_to_member covers them for curve members in mixed models.
acceptance_criteria: Every member in structure_01's results.json has a displacement envelope.
notes:
2026-10-10: confirmed on grid_of_beams. results.json 'members' entries for curve members hold only ifc_guid, id, type and status: no displacement, so a per-member check is impossible from the JSON.
2026-10-10 (aiz.40): on building_02 at 2 m, 601 of 664 surface members report a Live max that differs by more than 15% from the FRD maximum inside the member's bounding box (ground slab 2v2zbt...: JSON 14.0 mm, FRD 25.3 mm; wall 2QtsQwFP: JSON 18.8, FRD 2.9). This sent aiz.40 after the wrong slabs. Cause: _register_node_memberships() guesses expanded node numbers as original + k*N, which does not hold for S6/B32R expansions. Fix idea, verified on the file: the FRD element block (3C) keeps the input element labels (18165 elements: 2395 C3D20 for beams, 15655 C3D15 for shells, 115 links), so member -> analysis_element_ids -> FRD connectivity -> FRD nodes is exact, for beams too. Acceptance: also check building_02 per-member maxima against a bounding-box read of the FRD.
close_reason: Fixed. Results are attributed member -> final element set -> nodes of those elements in the FRD element block (ResultsParser.parse_element_nodes, ResultsExporter element_nodes). The writer now records each member's final elements (StructuralModel.set_analysis_elements) and no longer guesses expanded node numbers. Stresses are tagged with their load case (they were all under '_combined'). structure_01: all four members have an envelope, within 3% of Code_Aster at the member axis (8% on the faces of the pin-ended column). building_02: all 1304 members have displacement and stress for all three cases; the largest member value equals the global maximum per case; all 664 surfaces match a bounding-box read of the FRD.

title: Shell mesh convergence: replace linear S3 shells with quadratic elements
description: Slab results converge slowly and non-monotonically with mesh size: structure_01 0.375 / 0.472 / 0.561 mm at mesh 1.0 / 0.5 / 0.25 (reference 0.427), building_02 differs 2x between mesh 1.0 and 2.0. S3 is expanded by CalculiX to a 6-node wedge, which is very stiff in bending. Evaluate second-order Gmsh meshing with S6 (or quads with S8R) and B32R for beams, including merged joint nodes and knots, and CalculiX run time on building_02.
acceptance_criteria: structure_01 and a simply supported plate benchmark converge monotonically and reach within 5% of reference at a 0.5 m mesh.
close_reason: Second-order mesh is now the default (MeshingConfig.get_element_order, --element-order / element_order=1 for linear): B32R beams and S6 shells, three-node U1 members split in two. Line3 nodes reordered for CalculiX. Simply supported plate benchmark added: S6 +0.4/+2.6/+3.3% at 1.0/0.5/0.25 m against Navier+Mindlin, S3 was -55/-42/-19%. structure_01 0.4288/0.4340/0.4359 mm against 0.4273 (needed aiz.27, aiz.32, aiz.33 as well). building_02 at 2 m: 200 s, 1.8 GB; 1 m does not fit in 5 GB (aiz.37). S8R and B32 were not adopted: B32 and B32R agree within 1%, S6 already meets the criteria.

title: Load cases accumulated: each step included the loads of all earlier steps
description: CalculiX keeps loads active from step to step unless a card carries OP=NEW. The writer emitted plain *CLOAD/*DLOAD per step, so load case N was reported as the sum of cases 1..N (verified with a two-step cantilever). In building_02 the 'Gravity' result equalled 'Extra_dead' plus self-weight.
close_reason: Every static step now starts with '*CLOAD, OP=NEW' and '*DLOAD, OP=NEW'. Unit test added.

title: Surface members silently used default steel instead of their IFC material
description: _create_surface_member looked for a material profile and required a .Material attribute, so a slab or wall associated with a plain IfcMaterial (the normal case) fell through to a hard-coded steel default (E 210 GPa, 7850 kg/m3) with no warning. In structure_01 the slab was 1000 times heavier and stiffer than its columns (IFC: E 210 MPa, 7.8 kg/m3). bcf had fixed this for curve members only.
close_reason: _get_surface_material() reads IfcMaterial, layer sets, constituent sets and profile sets; the steel default now logs a warning. structure_01 went from 8-17 mm to 0.38-0.56 mm (Code_Aster reference 0.43 mm).

title: Line supports were reduced to one node at the edge midpoint
description: IfcStructuralCurveConnection was converted to a point connection at its midpoint, so a wall-base or slab-edge line support restrained a single node.
close_reason: The extractor keeps the edge end points on connection.edge; find_connection_support_nodes() restrains every node on the segment. structure_01's wall base now has 5/9/17 support nodes at mesh 1.0/0.5/0.25.

title: Joints without a support condition were written as fully fixed supports
description: get_constrained_dofs() fell back on entity_type when a connection had no stiffness properties, so a member-to-member connection of type 'rigid' (e.g. the slab-to-wall line connection in structure_01, 49 connections in building_02) was fixed to ground in all six DOFs.
close_reason: A connection joining two or more real members with no AppliedCondition restrains nothing.

title: Rigid connections were pins: CalculiX ignores *EQUATION on rotational DOFs of beam/shell nodes
description: Root cause of aiz.15. Beams and shells are meshed with separate nodes and were joined by *EQUATION on DOF 1-6. CalculiX expands B31/S3 into solids, whose nodes have no rotational DOFs; equations on DOF 4-6 are accepted and do nothing. Test: two collinear B31 beams joined at coincident nodes by equations on 1-6 give exactly the same result as equations on 1-3 (a hinge: 1e8 m displacement), while a shared node gives the continuous-beam answer. *RIGID BODY and *MPC BEAM on such nodes are rejected (gen3dmpc). In building_02 a beam tied to slabs at both ends spun freely about its own axis. The old reason for not sharing nodes (gen3dnor memory overflow from knots) does not occur on ccx 2.23 with building_02.
close_reason: _merge_rigid_connection_nodes(): members without an end release share one node at each rigid connection (CalculiX builds a knot). Members that stop short of the joint (rigid end zones, up to 2 m) are bridged with stiff B31 link elements. Connection points landing inside or on the edge of a slab are seeded into the surface geometry so the shell mesh has a node there. DOF 4-6 equations are no longer written; released members stay pinned by DOF 1-3 equations, and a partial release now warns that it is analysed as a full pin.

title: Wrong second moments of area for I, L and C sections
description: Found by the pipeline benchmarks (aiz.4). I-section weak-axis inertia used tw*(h-2tf)^3/12 for the web instead of (h-2tf)*tw^3/12: 6.55e-5 instead of 2.67e-5 m4 for a 200x400 I (2.5 times too stiff). C-section formulas cubed the wrong flange dimension and used wrong lever arms. L-section formulas were dimensionally inconsistent (t*cy^2 added to a length^4 term) and returned principal moments while the section is written in geometric axes.
close_reason: I, T, L and C now use one exact routine, Section._inertia_of_rectangles (parallel-axis sum over rectangles). L values are about the geometric centroidal axes; the product of inertia is still not modelled. Hand-checked unit tests in tests/unit/domain/test_section_inertia.py.

title: Point supports restrained every node within 0.1 m; point loads applied in full to each
description: Found by the pipeline benchmarks (aiz.4). write_boundary_conditions and _collect_boundary_condition_dofs used find_nodes_at_position(tolerance=0.1), which returns all nodes inside the radius. With element size at or below 0.1 m the neighbouring node was fixed too: cantilever_01 at mesh 0.1 fixed nodes at x=0 and x=0.1, giving 0.245 mm instead of 0.281 mm, and a pinned support restrained at two adjacent nodes becomes a clamp. write_point_load used the same search and *CLOAD on a node set applies the full force to every node, so a load could be multiplied.
close_reason: New find_support_nodes(): nearest node within tolerance plus nodes coincident with it (beam and shell meshes keep separate nodes at one point). Point loads go to the single nearest node. Benchmarks run at 0.05 m mesh.

title: Beam cross-sections were rotated 90 degrees: strong and weak axes swapped
description: Found by the pipeline benchmarks (aiz.4). cantilever_01 (0.2 x 0.4 rectangle, Axis=+Z, so depth vertical) deflected 1.107 mm under self-weight: the weak-axis answer. The strong-axis value is 0.281 mm, and IfcOpenShell's own Code_Aster reference (examples/analysis-models/models/cantilever_01/*.comm: HY=0.2, HZ=0.4, VECT_Y=(0,1,0)) agrees the depth is vertical. Two causes: (1) the native B31 path never used the IFC orientation at all; _split_beam_sets_by_orientation took a purely geometric normal from _compute_element_normal, and RECT was written width-first while CalculiX measures the first dimension along the given direction. (2) the U1 path passed the IFC local y as the section 1 direction with I11=Iy, but CalculiX pairs I11 with loads along the 1 direction. c9l had only changed _get_beam_normal, which the native path does not reach.
close_reason: Both paths now give CalculiX the IFC local z (Axis) as the section 1 direction, with depth-first RECT dimensions and I11=Iy. Geometric default is used only for members with no local_axis. Verified by strong and weak axis benchmarks for rectangular (B31) and I (U1) sections. title: Beam section forces in results.json via CalculiX 2D output (SECTION FORCES)
description:
Implement the finding of the spike aiz.3. Stock ccx 2.23 writes beam section forces when the step requests '*NODE FILE, OUTPUT=2D' and '*EL FILE, OUTPUT=2D, SECTION FORCES' with 'S'. The FRD then lists the original beam nodes (not the expanded brick nodes) and its STRESS block carries, per beam node: col1 shear along local 1, col2 shear along local 2, col3 axial N, col4 torque, col5 moment about 1, col6 moment about 2. Verified on a cantilever (tip load 1000 N, axial 500 N): V=1000, N=500 exactly; M is extrapolated to nodes, so end values are off on coarse meshes (864 vs 1000 at the root with 4 elements, exact at midspan).

Constraints found: (1) OUTPUT=3D and SECTION FORCES are mutually exclusive, and OUTPUT applies to the whole file. (2) In 2D mode shell stresses are averaged through the thickness, so bending stress disappears (plate strip: SXX ~0 instead of 7e6 Pa). Shell stress therefore has to come from elsewhere: '*EL PRINT' integration-point stresses in the .dat, or a second ccx run in 3D mode. (3) The current request '*EL FILE, ELSET=..., SF' is not valid CalculiX (SF is a fluid variable; ELSET is not an *EL FILE parameter) and _find_beam_elset() returns None for the example models anyway, so nothing was ever requested. (4) 2D output reports displacements on the real INP node ids, which makes node-to-member mapping exact and changes what the FRD parser and visualiser see. (5) U1 elements with 2D output are untested.
acceptance_criteria: A B31 cantilever and a simply supported beam run through the pipeline report N, V, M per member in results.json matching statics within a stated tolerance; shell members still report bending stress; utilisation is populated for B31 members; example-model baselines re-measured.
notes: 2026-10-10 (31a): members analysed as equivalent rectangles (domain_model.equivalent_section_members; section_model in results.json) have no stress in results.json. Their stresses must come from section forces and the true section moduli, so this bead now also unblocks stress for every non-rectangular section. Note for the calculation: the element's material is scaled (MAT_EQ_*), so use forces, not CalculiX stresses.
close_reason: Done, by a different route than planned: no 2D output mode and no second run. Section forces are integrated from the 3D stresses already in the FRD (analysis/section_forces.py): at each cross-section of an expanded beam element that has nodes, nodal stresses are interpolated over the rectangle (8-node serendipity or bilinear) and integrated in the frame the writer recorded (StructuralModel.beam_section_frames). Shell stresses are untouched. results.json: section_forces envelope per member and load case (max |N|, |T|, |Mf1|, |Mf2|, |Vf1|, |Vf2|), max_normal_stress_Pa from the real section combined per cross-section, utilisation_ratio where the material has a yield stress (YieldStress now extracted). Benchmarks: cantilever V, M, sigma < 0.1%; I-section as equivalent rectangle sigma < 0.1% both axes; fixed-fixed beam V < 0.1%, M 0.4% at 8 elements; portal_01 joint equilibrium to 4 digits. building_02: all 640 beams, same run time, +150 MB. The invalid '*EL FILE, ELSET, SF' request and _find_beam_elset are removed. Not done: signed forces and diagrams along the member; a simply supported beam case (no pinned-support benchmark exists yet, aiz.20).

title: [bug] Overlapping-geometry members lose elements when one side is retyped to U1
description:
building_01a and portal_01 fail CalculiX entirely: 8 integration tests fail with
'ERROR reading *BEAM SECTION: *BEAM SECTION can only be used for beam elements'
naming specific element IDs (e.g. 30, 36, 37, 40, 105 in building_01a).

ROOT CAUSE (traced in unified_calculix_writer.py):
1. mesh_mapper.py's shared-element-assignment fallback (~line 190-210, logged as
   'sharing N elements with another member (overlapping geometry)') lets TWO
   members claim the same element IDs in their respective self.element_sets
   entries when geometry overlaps (e.g. an I-section column embedded in a RECT
   member's span).
2. _identify_and_retype_u1_members() (line 431) retypes ALL of a U1-needing
   member's elem_ids to type 'U1' in the shared self.elements dict, including
   elements it only owns via the sharing fallback — with no check that another
   (non-U1) member also claims that same element ID.
3. _write_elements() (line 624) explicitly skips writing any element whose type
   is now 'U1' ('U1 elements are written individually ... inside _write_sections()
   — skip them here'), deferring their *ELEMENT card to _write_sections().
4. _write_sections() (line 999) iterates domain_model.members in order and has a
   dedup guard (line 1018-1027): if a member's element set intersects
   already_sectioned_elements, the member's ENTIRE section is skipped with a
   'skipping duplicate section' warning.
5. If the non-U1 (RECT) member happens to be processed BEFORE the U1 member in
   domain_model.members order, it claims the shared element ID into
   already_sectioned_elements and writes a *BEAM SECTION, SECTION=RECT ELSET
   that still lists the shared element ID (its element_sets entry was computed
   BEFORE retyping and is never filtered afterward).
6. When the U1 member is processed later, the dedup guard sees the shared
   element already claimed and skips the U1 member's section entirely — so the
   shared element's *ELEMENT card (which only gets written from the U1 path) is
   NEVER emitted anywhere in the file.

Net effect: elements retyped to U1 via sharing end up referenced by a stale RECT
*BEAM SECTION ELSET but are never defined by any *ELEMENT card in the .inp file.
CalculiX rejects the reference.

Confirmed via manual trace on tests/integration data:
- Ran examples/analysis-models/ifcFiles/building_01a.ifc through the CLI,
  inspected generated analysis.inp: elements 30, 36, 37, 40, 105, 106, 107, 108
  are referenced by *ELSET MEMBER_M10/M13/M14/M18(+_ORI1 variants) but do not
  appear in ANY *ELEMENT block (verified by parsing every *ELEMENT block in the
  file with a script — confirmed absent from B31, S3, and all U1_Mxx blocks).
- This predates the most recent commits; reproduced identically on commit
  8f87516 (before the c9l/6al beam-normal and warnings-channel fixes), so it is
  a pre-existing bug, not a regression from this session's earlier work.

REPRODUCE:
  python -m ifc_structural_mechanics.cli analyze \
    examples/analysis-models/ifcFiles/building_01a.ifc --output /tmp/b01a
  (fails with return code 201, BEAM SECTION errors for elements 30/36/37/40/105)

  Also affects portal_01 (4 test failures in
  tests/integration/test_results_json.py::TestPortal01ResultsJson).

DESIGN SKETCH (not yet implemented):
Likely fix: when _identify_and_retype_u1_members() retypes a shared element,
either (a) split ownership so the non-U1 member's element_sets entry drops the
now-U1 element before _write_sections() runs, or (b) make the dedup guard in
_write_sections() re-derive already_sectioned_elements from self.elements'
actual current type rather than first-claim-wins, ensuring whichever member
matches the element's final type is the one that writes it. Needs a regression
test using an IFC model with a RECT member and an overlapping I-section member
sharing mesh elements (mirrors building_01a's actual geometry).
close_reason:
Fixed in unified_calculix_writer.py with two changes:
1. _identify_and_retype_u1_members() now strips elements retyped to U1 from
   every non-U1 member's element_sets entry once retyping is complete, so a
   native (RECT/CIRC/etc.) member sharing mesh elements with an overlapping
   U1 (I/T/L/C-section) member no longer references those elements in its own
   *BEAM SECTION ELSET.
2. _write_sections()'s dedup guard for overlapping-geometry members now
   subtracts already-claimed elements from a member's set and writes a
   section for whatever remains, instead of skipping the member's entire
   section on any overlap. This fixes the case where a member sharing only a
   few elements with an earlier-processed member (e.g. the building_01a
   "hub" member sharing elements with 5 other members) was losing ALL of its
   elements, not just the shared ones.

Added regression tests in test_overlapping_member_fallback.py:
- TestU1RetypeStripsSharedElements (2 tests) — exercises the retyping fix
  directly.
- TestSectionDeduplication::test_partial_overlap_writes_remaining_elements —
  exercises the partial-overlap write fix.

Verified against the real building_01a/portal_01 example models:
- portal_01: all 4 previously-failing integration tests now pass.
- building_01a: the original *BEAM SECTION "not a beam element" errors are
  gone; CalculiX now proceeds past input-deck reading into STEP execution.
  It hits a DIFFERENT, unrelated, pre-existing bug there (filed separately as
  eez — CalculiX 'gen3delem: first thickness ... is zero').

Full non-slow suite: 729 passed, 1 pre-existing unrelated failure (ziq,
buckling benchmark). No regressions.

title: Warn when a cross-section is approximated with loss of fidelity affecting results
description:
Several section approximations silently change the analysis model and are never reported to the user (no logger.warning on the success path, nothing in result['warnings']):

1. IfcAsymmetricIShapeProfileDef -> averaged to a SYMMETRIC I (properties_extractor.py:586, lines 613-614 average top/bottom flanges; stored as section_type='i'). Asymmetry is lost.
2. The U1 SECTION=GENERAL card forces the product of inertia xi12 to 0.0 (unified_calculix_writer.py:968) and supports no offset/eccentricity. For L (angle) sections the true principal axes are rotated (non-zero product of inertia), so bending about the principal axes is not reproduced.
3. Unknown / unsupported profiles fall back to a default section (properties_extractor.py:486) or default to U1 GENERAL (unified_calculix_writer.py:422). The extraction case logs to logger but nothing reaches result['warnings']; the U1-default case only logs info.

Per project policy, any fundamental limitation that affects analysis results MUST raise a user-visible warning. These do not.
design: Record provenance on the Section at extraction time (e.g. a Section.approximations: List[str] or flags like was_asymmetric / product_of_inertia_dropped / is_default_fallback) so the loss is not forgotten once the profile is reduced to scalars. Then, mirroring _validate_model (api/structural_analysis.py:123), add a post-extraction pass that walks domain_model.members and appends a warning dict (message, severity='warning', entity_type, ccx_id=None, domain_id=member.id, plus ifc_guid) to result['warnings'] for each approximated section. Also emit logger.warning and, optionally, an '** *** SECTION WARNING:' comment in the .inp (same pattern as STABILITY WARNING at writer.py:514) for traceability. Each warning must name the IFC GlobalId and member id. Depends on the warnings-channel fix so the messages are not later overwritten.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Tests written FIRST (one per case): asymmetric-I model, L-section model, and unknown/unsupported-profile model each produce a warning in result['warnings'] naming the offending member/GlobalId.
2. Symmetric sections that are NOT approximated (RECT, CIRC, PIPE, BOX, symmetric I) produce NO such warning.
3. Warning text states the concrete effect (e.g. 'asymmetric I-section approximated as symmetric — section properties and neutral-axis location are approximate').
4. Linters clean; existing tests pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: result[warnings] overwritten after CalculiX run — pre-analysis warnings silently dropped
description:
api/structural_analysis.py:124 does result['warnings'].extend(validation_warnings) to record pre-analysis model-validation warnings. But line 176 then does result['warnings'] = parse_result.get('warnings', []), an ASSIGNMENT that REPLACES the list — discarding every warning accumulated before CalculiX ran (validation warnings, and any future extraction/meshing warnings). The CLI prints result['warnings'] (cli/commands.py:310), so these dropped warnings never reach the user.

This makes the warnings channel unreliable and is a prerequisite for surfacing section-modelling limitation warnings.
design: Change line 176 from assignment to extend (result['warnings'].extend(parse_result.get('warnings', []))). Audit the whole function for any other place that reassigns rather than appends to result['warnings'] or result['errors']. Consider initialising parse-stage warnings into a local then extending once.

title: Beam section normal uses longitudinal axis instead of cross-section orientation
description:
`_get_beam_normal()` (meshing/unified_calculix_writer.py:143) returns `member.local_axis[0]` as the CalculiX beam normal. But `get_1D_orientation()` (ifc/entity_identifier.py:808) builds local_axis as [xAxis, yAxis, zAxis] where xAxis = point2 - point1 = the LONGITUDINAL beam axis, and the real IFC orientation (.Axis) is stored in local_axis[2]. So the returned 'normal' is parallel to the beam axis by construction.

Consequences:
- U1/GENERAL path orthogonalises the normal against the beam axis (writer.py:947), which collapses to ~zero and falls back to a CANONICAL perpendicular (global Y->X->Z), discarding the true IFC orientation.
- Native B31 path has no orthogonalisation and can emit a normal parallel to the axis (degenerate; vertical-column crash class).
- The IFC .Axis vector is exactly what encodes section orientation AND rotation about the longitudinal axis for IfcStructuralCurveMember, so honouring it fixes both off-axis orientation and rotation-on-axis fidelity.

Symmetric sections (circle/square/pipe) are unaffected; directional/asymmetric sections (rectangle, I, T, C) are silently mis-oriented, which can swap strong/weak axis.
design: Fix _get_beam_normal to return a vector PERPENDICULAR to the beam axis, derived from the IFC orientation: prefer local_axis[1] (yAxis) or local_axis[2] (zAxis, from IFC .Axis), orthogonalised against the actual beam axis. The geometry-fallback branch is already correct (it computes a true perpendicular) and should be retained for members with no .Axis. Keep the existing U1 orthogonalisation as a safety net. Note: this honours IfcStructuralCurveMember.Axis; per-profile rotation via IfcParameterizedProfileDef.Position is a separate, rarely-used mechanism for structural members and is out of scope here.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A regression test is written FIRST and fails against current code: build a CurveMember with a known I-section and a known .Axis (e.g. horizontal beam with web vertical), assert the written *BEAM SECTION line-2 normal is perpendicular to the beam axis AND aligned with the IFC .Axis-derived direction (not a canonical fallback).
2. A second test covers a member whose .Axis is rotated about the longitudinal axis (e.g. section rotated 90 deg) and asserts the written normal rotates accordingly.
3. Both native (RECT) and U1 (GENERAL) section paths produce a normal perpendicular to the beam axis.
4. Existing orientation/section tests still pass; black/isort/flake8/ruff clean.
close_reason: Closed

title: Number warnings and errors, and document each so users can look them up
description:
Raised 2026-10-18. What reaches a user today is free text: about 45 places add warnings (23 in unified_calculix_writer.py, 8 in boundary_condition_handling.py, the rest in extractors, plausibility, output_parser, results_parser, structural_analysis) and about 184 raise a typed error (AnalysisError, MeshingError, ModelExtractionError, ResultProcessingError). Warnings are dicts {message, severity, entity_type, ccx_id, domain_id} filled unevenly (domain_id often None, entity ids only in the text). Errors carry the same fields on StructuralAnalysisError but the message is the whole of it in result['errors']. A tool (Bonsai, a report) can only match on wording, which changes.

Proposal:
- A registry module (utils/messages.py) with one entry per kind: a stable code (e.g. W-SUP-003 / E-MSH-001, or plain W101/E201 grouped by stage: extraction, meshing, writer/supports, joints, loads, solver, results, plausibility), a title, severity, and a template. Codes are never reused or renumbered.
- _warn_user, _warn_model, Extractor warnings, solver_warnings, plausibility and every raise go through it; each record gains 'code' and a list of IFC GlobalIds ('ifc_guids') rather than ids embedded in the text, so a viewer can highlight the entities.
- The text keeps the house style: says what was found, what it means for the results, and what to do; one record per kind with a count and the first few ids (CLAUDE.md principle 6).

title: results.json for Bonsai overlays and PDF reports: missing data and a schema outsiders can use
description:
Assessed 2026-10-18 against schema 1.9. The schema is described in the docstring of export/results_exporter.py: thorough on meaning (signs, axes, where reactions and moments come from), but it is prose inside an internal module, its example still says 1.8, and there is no JSON Schema, no example file and no page in docs/. What a Bonsai overlay or a calculation report would need and does not get:

Missing from the file:
- Warnings. They are in analyze_ifc's return value only, not in results.json; a report must state every approximation (CLAUDE.md principle 6), and a viewer should flag members named in them.
- Run settings: mesh size, element order, strict connections, open-section model, gravity, CalculiX version, library version, input file name/hash, date. A report has to state them and a viewer has to know whether results are stale.
- Deflected shape. Members have their largest displacement only; drawing a deformed curve member needs displacements along it (like section_force_diagrams: distance_m plus ux,uy,uz and rotations, per case/combination), and a surface member needs nodal values on some mesh (or at least points keyed to its outline) for a contour.
- Surface member results beyond maxima: no plate moments, membrane forces or shear per unit length, which are what a slab or wall is designed from.
- Buckling mode shapes (only factors).
- What status ok/warning/fail tests: the limits are not in the file or the docstring.

Documentation:
- Move the schema to docs/results_schema.md (or a JSON Schema in the package, validated in a test against example outputs), keep the docstring a pointer.
- Ship a small example results.json (portal_01 with its combinations) for consumers to develop against.
- Say what versions mean (additive minor bumps vs breaking) and keep a changelog of 1.0 to 1.9.

Settle with Bonsai (IfcOpenShell issue 9866) which of these they want before adding data: the deflected shape and surface fields enlarge the file.
notes: 2026-10-18, asked by Bruno: could results.json one day be exported as IFC structural results (IfcStructuralResultGroup per load case/combination with ResultForLoadGroup, IfcStructuralPointReaction on connections, IfcStructuralCurveReaction with an IfcStructuralLoadConfiguration on members; portal_01.ifc is an example of the form)? Reactions per support (ifc_guid, force+moment, per case and combination) and section force diagrams along members (distance_m, signed N/V/M/T) map directly. Missing: displacements along members and at connections (IfcStructuralLoadSingleDisplacement), surface member fields, the load groups' GlobalIds for load cases (combinations have ifc_guid), the axes the diagrams are in as vectors, and theory type/linearity for the result group.
close_reason: Schema 1.10: results.json has run (versions, input SHA-256, settings), warnings (with GlobalIds; W-SEC-001/002, W-LOD-004/005 and W-RES-001 now carry them) and limits. Schema moved to docs/results_schema.md with versioning rules and a 1.0-1.10 changelog; example docs/examples/beam_01_results.json (portal_01 has no combinations), kept in step by tests. Deflected shapes, surface fields and mode shapes moved to 94g.13 pending Bonsai.

title: Surface supports (IfcStructuralSurfaceConnection), rigid and elastic
description: Split from aiz.58 (2). Face from the IfcFaceSurface/IfcFace of its Reference representation (in placement axes), axes from its plane (IfcPlane Position, else polygon normal and first edge). IfcBoundaryFaceCondition gives TranslationalStiffnessByArea X/Y/Z (N/m^3, bool for rigid/free). Geometry: intersect the face with each surface member it lies on and fragment the member with it so the mesh conforms to its outline. Writer: rigid directions as for a line support on every shell node inside the face; finite ones as springs with HRZ-lumped areas (S6 corners 3/57, mids 16/57 of the element; S3 1/3). Reactions: solver force at rigid nodes plus k u at springs.
notes: 2026-10-17 done: extraction (_build_surface_connection: face from IfcFace/IfcFaceSurface edge or poly loop, axes from the IfcPlane Position), geometry (_surface_support_pieces fragments the members along the outline), find_nodes_in_face(). slab_01 on k = 1e7 N/m3: reaction q A exactly, settlement q/k to 1% (springs lumped HRZ, load by work). Half the slab held rigidly: reaction and its moment exact, free half 193 mm against q L^4/8D + M l/D = 194 mm (normals turn against transverse shear inside the held area). Not covered: a surface support under a wall or a sloping slab; a beam lying in a rigidly held area.
close_reason: Closed

title: U1 members split into two-node elements have no node at their ends (--open-sections user-element fails on portal_01)
description: Found during aiz.83: analyze_ifc(portal_01, open_sections='user_element') raised MeshingError 'The mesh has no node for 3 member end(s) at their connection' on main (4c9f416). _split_quadratic_u1_elements() gives the second half of each three-node line a new id; _geometry_element_sets (aiz.87), which _find_connection_nodes_at_location() goes by, still listed the first halves only, so the end node of every U1 member was missing from its node set. The U1 cantilever benchmarks did not catch it: their only connection is at the start node. Fix: add the second halves to every geometry set listing the first. Tests: TestQuadraticUserElements.test_member_geometry_keeps_its_end_node, TestPortalAgainstTheResultsInItsFile.test_user_elements_deflect_as_the_native_beams (passes on 2.21 and 2.23). portal_01 U1: 2.06 mm default, 2.18 mm at 0.25 m, as documented.
close_reason: Fixed in _split_quadratic_u1_elements(); regression tests added.

title: Shear diagram has false steps under a load that varies along its member
description: ResultsExporter._restore_jumps() takes the median slope between element middles as the normal one for the whole member ('a force normally changes by the same amount per metre all along the member'). Under a line load that varies (LINEAR/POLYGONAL since aiz.82, SINUS/PARABOLA since aiz.58) or covers part of the member that is not so, and every element end whose slope differs from the median by more than _JUMP_FRACTION gets a step that is not there. Measured 2026-10-12, 4 m simply supported beam, 0.1 m square, 0.25 m mesh, 3 kN/m peak: sine half wave, the two values at an element end are 5% either side of the exact shear near the supports and 14% near midspan; envelope max_Vf2_N 3949.5 N for a reaction of 3819.7 N (3.4% high). Triangular load: 5 to 8% either side, 15% near the zero of the shear. Uniform load: exact. Element middles are right to 0.2%; moments, reactions and deflections are not affected (moment 0.3% high). Fix: judge each element end against the slopes of its neighbours, not the member's median; must stay right for point loads at adjacent nodes and exact for a linear variation, ends of the member included. Add shear assertions to TestLoadThatVariesAlongABeam (none of its cases checks the diagram except the point forces).
close_reason: Jumps are now found from each element by itself (its middle against the mean of its two ends), added up along the member and told apart by the line most of seven cross-sections are on; nothing is assumed of the load. No false shear step under triangular, part, sine or parabolic loads at 0.25 and 0.5 m meshes; shear assertions added to TestLoadThatVariesAlongABeam; unit tests for point loads under varying loads, at adjacent nodes, and for members in line.

title: A support that leaves rotations free hinges every member that meets there
description: analyze_connection_type() returns 'hinge' for a connection whose AppliedCondition has a free rotation, and the writer (_write_connections, _build_release_hinges, the mechanism check) then releases all three rotations of every member at it. The condition of a connection is what it holds against the ground; how a member is joined to it is the AppliedCondition of its IfcRelConnectsStructuralMember. So a beam continuous over a pinned support (two members meeting at it, no member-side release) is analysed as two simply supported beams, with no warning. Found while fixing aiz.72: a straight run of four members with ball supports at two inner joints came out with its overhangs detached. No example file has a support with free rotations joining two members, so no reference changes. Fix: the type of a connection must not depend on its support condition.
close_reason: analyze_connection_type() gives the type of the entity only; a support condition no longer makes a connection a hinge. Two 4 m spans over three pinned supports, 10 kN mid-span each: moment over the support 0 before, 7496 N.m now for 7500; under the loads 10000 before, 6252 now for 6250; deflection 8.00 mm before, 3.42 now. No example model has such a support joining two members. TestBeamContinuousOverASupport. Passes on ccx 2.21 too.

Fixed: factors add, Coefficient multiplies, and a combination that cannot be formed is left out with a warning naming it. title: Analyse plane trusses and frames
description: Textbook 2D trusses and frames (the Bonsai author's first use) have nothing restraining them out of their plane, and all-pinned joints leave every member free to spin about its axis and each joint free to rotate. Not yet run here: first establish what happens today (singular solve, garbage, or held with warnings) on a plane truss and a plane frame authored in Bonsai, in the X-Z plane. Then decide between detecting a planar model and restraining out-of-plane translation and in-plane-axis rotations with a warning, or an explicit option (--plane). Supports must not be invented silently (CLAUDE.md principle 6): whatever is added is reported. Benchmarks: a statically determinate truss (member forces by method of joints, joint deflection by virtual work) and a portal frame, in test_pipeline_benchmarks.py. Truss members also need axial-only behaviour to come out right with releases at both ends.
close_reason: Done 2026-10-12. Today's behaviour measured first: forces right, displacements wrong (truss on X/Z supports 19x; portal fixed in plane only 13.3 mm for 9.9; beam 8.5 for 7.6), no useful warning. Decision: detect, not an option. analysis/plane_structure.py recognises a plane structure (curve members, plane parallel to two global axes, loads in it) and counts unrestrained out-of-plane movements by rigid-body kinematics; if any, every node is held across the plane and spinning members/runs are held at a pinned end or support, with one warning. Linear static only; models that stand up are untouched. Benchmarks: truss by method of joints (4 figures) and virtual work (0.5%), portal pinned and fixed by hand (0.2% moments, 0.5% sway), held portal equals fully fixed portal. Not done: planes not parallel to global axes, plane models with surface members, models authored in Bonsai itself.

title: Solve and report load combinations
description: LoadsExtractor reads LOAD_COMBINATION groups and IfcRelAssignsToGroupByFactor factors into StructuralModel.load_combinations, but nothing after that uses them: no step is written and results.json lists load cases only. Bonsai stage 2 will author combinations. For linear static analysis a combination is the factored sum of its cases' results, so it can be formed in the exporter without another solver step (displacements, reactions, section force diagrams; envelopes and stresses need recomputing from the summed fields, not summing maxima). Decide: superpose, or write a step per combination. Refuse or warn for buckling. Validate with a two-case beam against hand values and against a single case holding the factored loads. Bump schema_version.
close_reason: Done 2026-10-12. Decision: superpose, not a step per combination (building_02 has 17). analysis/superposition.combine_results() adds the linear raw results (displacement vectors, stress components, section force records, support node forces, step loads); ResultsExporter runs on the sum, one combination at a time, so non-linear quantities are recomputed. results.json schema 1.2: load_combinations, by_load_combination, combination_envelope, section_force_diagrams_by_combination. Buckling: warning, none. Validated on beam_01 with two cases: hand values, and one case holding the factored loads (1e-6). building_02: +100 s, 5 -> 44 MB.

title: Report reactions per support in results.json
description: results.json has only global_reactions totals per load case. Bonsai's overlay and calculation reports need the reaction at each support: forces and moments per load case, keyed to the connection's GlobalId, in global axes and in the support's own axes (ConditionCoordinateSystem), for point and line supports. Mind: the force an MPC carries into a restrained node is reported at the dependent node (bd memory calculix-beam-expansion-facts 5); U1 reactions have the wrong sign (aiz.19); the reaction leaves out the load share landing on the restrained node itself. Check by summing per-support reactions against global_reactions and against statics for beam_01, portal_01 and a propped cantilever. Bump schema_version and document the new block in results_exporter.py and README.
close_reason: results.json schema 1.1: supports[] with force and moment per load case, keyed to GlobalId, in global axes and the support's own; global_reactions gains applied_load_N and imbalance_N. Forces are the solver's less the loads applied at the support nodes (reactions now equal applied loads to 3e-7 on every example at any mesh). Moments from member end section forces (0.1-0.2% on cantilever_01 and beam_01); absent where a slab is clamped or a member runs on past the support. On CalculiX 2.21 the solver's forces at rotation-holding supports are wrong: detected, replaced by member end forces where possible, marked unreliable otherwise, with a warning. Fast suite passes on 2.23 (1045) and on 2.21 in a container (9 solver-reaction tests skipped).

title: Serve Bonsai's structural analysis work (IfcOpenShell issue 9866)

A PyNite backend for frames and trusses is proposed alongside CalculiX. title: Section.torsional_constant of a solid rectangle was 16 times too large
description: domain/property.py used Roark's half-side formula with whole sides, and with long and short swapped: a 0.3 m square gave 2.25 a^4 instead of 0.1406 a^4. Nothing read it for rectangles until aiz.53 (it was in Section.as_dict()). Fixed 2026-10-11 with test_rectangular_torsion_constant_is_saint_venants (square, 1:2, 2:1, 1:10 against the tabulated beta, 0.5%).

title: Unreadable results gave status success
description: analyze_ifc turned any failure to parse the results or write results.json into a warning and returned 'success'; a result file with no displacements parsed as an empty set; output_files lost its results_json entry. Two mocked API tests passed only because of this. Now ResultProcessingError -> status failed. Also the mesh writer created an empty file in place of a mesh under pytest, and an unknown meshing algorithm became Delaunay.

title: ifc-analysis --json-output always failed with exit code 99
description: The result dictionary holds the StructuralModel, which json.dumps cannot serialise; Gmsh also wrote its log to standard output. Now the model and parsed result objects are left out and Gmsh is silenced in JSON mode. Test: TestJsonOutput in tests/unit/cli/test_commands.py.
close_reason: Found and fixed with aiz.59

title: Member Axis was turned wrongly by a rotated placement
description: members_extractor rotated the 3x3 local axes as R.M (matrix product) instead of turning each axis by R, so a member under a rotated ObjectPlacement got wrong section axes. Supports and loads ignored their placement altogether, and a point connection with no ConditionCoordinateSystem kept global axes under a rotated placement. Found and fixed with aiz.57; covered by test_object_placement.py.
close_reason: Found and fixed with aiz.57

title: Member placement offset is not converted to SI units
description: entity_identifier.get_transformation() reads the placement Location with get_coordinate() and no unit scale. MembersExtractor scales the member geometry to metres first and then applies the transformation, so in a file in millimetres a member with a non-zero ObjectPlacement is shifted by 1000 times too little or too much. ConnectionsExtractor transforms first and scales after, which is consistent. Also: point connections never have their ObjectPlacement applied (only curve connections do). No example model has a non-identity placement on a member, so this is unverified: build a mm model with a placed member and compare.
close_reason: Confirmed and fixed. get_transformation() now follows the whole PlacementRelTo chain and returns its offset in metres; get_item_transformation() applies it to member geometry and Axis, connection positions/edges/condition axes, release axes, load positions and forces in GLOBAL_COORDS. Verified: beam_01 (mm), portal_01 (inch), structure_01 (m), building_01 (mm) moved 13.5 m and turned a quarter turn give the shipped deflections and reactions (TestPlacedModel, tests/unit/ifc/test_object_placement.py).

title: Mesh and writer fallbacks changed the model without telling the user
description: Found in aiz.12. A Gmsh point, line, surface or fragment that failed was logged and skipped (members then share no nodes); a mesh without physical groups had its elements dealt out round-robin; members overlapping others lost elements with only a log line; members with no elements had their section skipped; spring and unknown connection types were ignored; results failing validation were skipped. Now MeshingError, or one aggregated warning in the results.
close_reason: Fixed in the aiz.12 round, with tests

title: Hollow rectangular section had a torsion constant of the wrong dimension
description: domain/property.py computed 2 t (bo-t)(ho-t)^2/(bo+ho-2t), one factor short of Bredt's 4 Am^2 t / perimeter (m^3, not m^4). Nothing in the default analysis read it until aiz.50 matched torsion for closed sections. Fixed, with a unit test.
close_reason: Fixed: Bredt formula, unit test

title: Export signed section forces and diagrams along each member
description: results.json gives only the envelope of magnitudes per member and load case. The records behind it (parsed_results['section_forces']: element, cross-section position -1/0/1, N, Vf1, Vf2, T, Mf1, Mf2) have what a diagram needs, but signs follow each element's own direction and Gmsh does not order elements along a member. Needed: a consistent member direction (start to end of the IFC edge), station distance along the member, sign convention documented, and a detail-level section in results.json (VISION 'Detail' level). Also min/max signed N, since tension and compression are not the same check.
close_reason: Done. Each element's frame is turned to the member's direction (first to last point of its geometry) so signs agree along a member; records carry the distance from the member's start. results.json: section_axes (x, 1, 2), section_force_diagrams per load case (distance_m, N_N, Vf1_N, Vf2_N, T_Nm, Mf1_Nm, Mf2_Nm, signed), and max_tension_N / max_compression_N in the summary. Convention documented in analysis/section_forces.py and the exporter. Steps smoothed by nodal averaging (shear under a point load) are restored for N, V, T from element-middle cross-sections on members of 4+ quadratic elements. Benchmarks: cantilever V and M at all 121 cross-sections within 1%; fixed-fixed beam -P/2 | +P/2 at midspan and +-PL/8. building_02 results.json is 7.2 MB. Not done: jumps in bending moment (applied point moments), short members and linear elements stay averaged; a per-node displacement detail level.

title: Area load lost where a surface member lies inside another
description: building_01: a 1 m2 landing lies inside the floor slab. After fragment the elements belong to the floor, the landing has none, and its loads were skipped at debug level (floor finishing reaction 12.0 kN against 13.5 by hand; Live 279.94 against 282.0, including 60 N on a 0.02 m2 member inside the same slab). Fix: UnifiedCalculixWriter._load_element_sets() applies an area load to every shell element within the member's outline when its own elements do not cover it; a load on a member with no elements at all now warns. Reactions: 282000 and 13500 N exactly.
close_reason: Fixed; building_01 reactions equal the hand totals.

title: building_02: two slabs move 462 and 258 mm under Live, ten times their Extra_dead movement
description: At a 2 m mesh, after the load fix: slab 3X2H_kqe10Qe1jcV$KfFne (x 13.67-19.56, y 9.77-12.24, z 34.8, t 0.15) moves 462 mm under Live and 42.4 mm under Extra_dead; slab 0sHrjowjn9kP0wtnJgsrYZ (x 19.56-26.12, y 8.18-14.06, z 31.6, t 0.2) 258 and 23.7 mm. The ratio is 10.9 for both, although their own loads are 1.5 kPa against 1.2 and 3.4 kPa. Everything else is below 45 mm. So these two are carried along by something barely restrained (a near-mechanism), excited far more by the Live pattern. Live has two loads Extra_dead lacks: 16 kPa on a slab at z=3 and 20 kPa on slab 2IwP2EtiH8IO7mp_xwD4Jg at z=60.2, which sits over the same x-range as the first slab (lift or stair core?). Look at what connects these slabs to the rest: released column ends, wall edges, connections the writer could not resolve. Each run takes 3 minutes; cut the model down if possible. Related: aiz.28 (warn on implausible results).
close_reason: Cause found: not a mechanism. The bead named the wrong slabs (per-member values in results.json are wrong, see aiz.31); the 462 mm was the ground-floor slab at z=3 under 16 kPa, and 10.9 was simply its Live/Extra_dead load ratio. It was held at its four corners only. Fixed by tying beams to the slab they lie in (ifc_structural_mechanics-aiz.41). Live is now 25.8 mm at 2 m.

title: building_02 with quadratic shells: 1 m mesh exceeds 5 GB, results much softer than before
description: With S6/B32R (aiz.26) building_02 at a 2 m mesh takes about 200 s and 1.8 GB (was about 90 s with S3/B31). At 1 m (41751 S6, 93777 mid-surface nodes) CalculiX's SPOOLES factorisation needs more than the 5 GB this machine has and swaps indefinitely. Results at 2 m: Live 455 mm, Extra_dead 434 mm (317 mm of it horizontal), self-weight 118 mm; at 4 m: 385 / 319 / 101 mm. With linear shells at 1 m these were 99 / 252 / 25.5 mm, so the linear model was several times too stiff, and the answer still moves 15-35 % between 4 m and 2 m. Options: S8R quads (about 25 % fewer nodes), the iterative solver, coarser shells with local refinement, or --element-order 1 for a first look. The large horizontal movement under Extra_dead also deserves a look together with aiz.29.
notes:
2026-10-10, after the distributed-load fix (aiz.39): building_02 at 2 m gives Live 462, Extra_dead 42, self-weight 120 mm; at 4 m 395 / 36 / 103 mm. The horizontal movement under Extra_dead was the load bug and is gone. What is left here is memory at 1 m and the 17% change between 4 m and 2 m; the Live figure is aiz.40.
2026-10-10 (aiz.40): the softness was slabs spanning corner to corner. With beams tied to the slabs they lie in, 4 m vs 2 m is 24.0/25.8 (Live), 14.4/15.3 (Extra_dead), 15.7/16.8 mm (gravity): 7%. Time and memory unchanged (about 230 s with gravity, 1.8 GB at 2 m). What is left here is only the memory needed at 1 m.
2026-10-17: measured at 2 m on CalculiX 2.23: ccx alone with SPOOLES takes 60 s and 2.08 GB for the three static steps (the whole pipeline 3 min 54 s, 2.2 GB peak). SOLVER=ITERATIVE CHOLESKY uses 0.87 GB but does not converge: error 0.02-0.16 against a limit of 2.7e-5 after 3100 iterations (expanded thin shells are ill-conditioned). The iterative solvers are ruled out. Next to try: S8R quads (about 25% fewer nodes than S6 for the same size), measured on a plain plate first.
2026-10-17, plate 40 x 40 m at 0.5 m (simply supported, 0.25 m thick, uniform pressure), ccx 2.23 SPOOLES: S6 25921 nodes 1.07 GB 8.7 s, centre 2.5693 m; S8R 19521 nodes 0.89 GB 8.2 s, 2.5704 m (Navier 2.554). Quads save 17% of memory, not enough: at 2 m building_02 needs 2.08 GB in ccx, and four times the nodes at 1 m will need several times that whatever the shell. With stock CalculiX (SPOOLES only, iterative solvers do not converge on expanded shells) a 1 m mesh of building_02 does not fit in 5 GB. Remaining options are outside the code: a machine with more memory, or a CalculiX build with PaStiX/PARDISO.

title: Skew supports are not modelled
