title: Equivalent-stiffness RECT on B31 for non-native beam profiles (stock CalculiX)
description:
Give non-native beam profiles (I, asymmetric I, L, T, C, U, Z) a path that runs on
stock CalculiX in any model, by writing native B31 elements with a
stiffness-equivalent RECT section instead of U1 + SECTION=GENERAL.

Motivation: U1 members crash stock CalculiX whenever the model also contains any
other 1D/2D element (gen3delem bug, see ifc_structural_mechanics-eez and
patches/calculix-gen3delem-user-element.patch), which is most real building
models. Decision 2026-10-09: stay on stock CalculiX, so these sections need a
non-U1 path.

Approach:
- Per member, solve for RECT dimensions a, b and a scaled modulus E' so that EA,
  EI11 and EI22 equal the true section's values (three unknowns, three targets).
  Write a per-member material carrying E'.
- Scale the per-member density so rho*A (self-weight, mass) is correct.
- Do not report CalculiX stresses for these members. Compute stresses and
  utilisation in Python from SF section forces and the true section moduli.
- Select the path in converters/section_profiles.py (SECTION_REGISTRY) so the
  writer keeps a single decision point; keep U1 selectable for models where it
  is safe (see the U1 bead).
- Replace the existing safety-net RECT fallback in the B31 section writer
  (matches A and Iy only, warns) with this exact mapping.
- Keep the loss-of-fidelity warning (z96) but narrow it to what is still
  approximate: torsion and shear.

Known limitation: GJ cannot be matched independently because G is tied to E'
through Poisson's ratio. Matters for grids and torsion-sensitive frames.

Also check: the CalculiX manual may restrict SECTION=PIPE and SECTION=BOX to
B32R, while the registry writes them for B31.
acceptance_criteria: A model mixing an I-section beam with native-section members and shells runs on unpatched CalculiX; deflections and section forces match the analytical solution under point, distributed and gravity loads; utilisation uses true section moduli; black, isort, flake8 and ruff pass.
notes:
2026-10-09: see ifc_structural_mechanics-aiz.14 - even on a patched ccx, U1 members are pin-jointed to B31 members, so U1 is only correct in all-U1 models. See aiz.13 for how section forces are obtained on stock ccx.
2026-10-10: stiffness part DONE; left open only because it depends on aiz.13 for the stress part. Done: every section other than a solid rectangle (I, T, L, C, circular, hollow circular, hollow rectangular) is written as RECT a,b on a native beam element with its own material: a=sqrt(12Iy/A), b=sqrt(12Iz/A), E and density scaled by A/(ab), orthotropic with G12, G13 set to the section's shear stiffness (CalculiX's expanded rectangle shears over its whole area, not 5/6). Default; --open-sections user-element keeps U1. Benchmarks: I cantilever 0.2% strong / 0.7% weak, fixed-fixed I beam 2.1% point load, <0.1% line load, slab on two I beams 0.8%, bar/tube/box 0.2%. building_01 solves: reactions 282.0 and 13.5 kN equal the hand totals. portal_01: 4.111 mm equivalent vs 4.120 mm U1 at 0.25 m. REMAINING: stresses and utilisation for these members from section forces and true section moduli (after aiz.13); results.json omits their stress and marks them section_model=equivalent_rectangle. Torsion is approximate (open: too stiff; thin closed: about half). The PIPE/BOX check asked for here found three bugs, fixed as aiz.44.
close_reason: Done. Stiffness part earlier today (see notes); stresses for these members now come from section forces and the real section (aiz.13): max_normal_stress_Pa and utilisation_ratio in results.json. Torsional stiffness remains approximate by construction.

title: [bug] Overlap resolution scattered across write sites causes double shell sections and DLOAD crashes
description: Follow-up from 51j and eez investigation: _write_sections()'s shell-section branch referenced the raw, unfiltered MEMBER_xxx elset instead of the deduped element set, so overlapping shell members could get covered by two *SHELL SECTION cards. Separately, boundary_condition_handling.py's DLOAD-writing code checked element_set_name not in element_sets (key presence) instead of checking non-emptiness, so a member that legitimately lost all its elements to an overlapping member during resolution still got a *DLOAD card referencing a never-written *ELSET, crashing CalculiX with 'ERROR reading *DLOAD: element set'.
acceptance_criteria: Overlap ownership resolved once via a single source-of-truth method (not re-implemented per write site); no double *SHELL SECTION coverage; DLOAD skips members with empty element sets after resolution; full test suite green.
close_reason:
Fixed in unified_calculix_writer.py and boundary_condition_handling.py:

1. Replaced the ad-hoc overlap dedup logic that had accumulated in
   _write_sections() (from the earlier 51j fix) with a single centralized
   method, _resolve_overlapping_element_sets(), called once in the pipeline
   right after _identify_and_retype_u1_members(). It mutates self.element_sets
   in place so every downstream consumer (raw *ELSET cards, orientation
   grouping, nodal thickness, node-membership registration, section writing)
   sees a consistent, non-overlapping assignment. _write_sections() itself is
   back to its pre-51j simplicity — it just reads the already-resolved sets.

2. Fixed two DLOAD-writing checks in boundary_condition_handling.py
   (lines ~1170, ~1270) that tested `element_set_name not in element_sets`
   (key presence) instead of `not element_sets.get(element_set_name)`
   (non-emptiness). A member losing all its elements to overlap resolution
   still has a (now-empty) dict entry, so the old check let a *DLOAD card
   through referencing an *ELSET that _write_element_sets() never actually
   writes (it skips empty lists) — CalculiX rejected the file with
   "ERROR reading *DLOAD: element set".

Rewrote the unit tests from 51j (TestSectionDeduplication) to target
_resolve_overlapping_element_sets() directly instead of _write_sections(),
plus a new no-overlap sanity test. Fixed a real regression this surfaced:
the interim per-write-site fix used elset names like MEMBER_M1_SHELL, which
broke tests/integration/test_element_member_mapping.py's naive
"MEMBER_" prefix matching (treated the raw and filtered elsets as two
different members' sets, flagging false overlap duplicates) — the
centralized fix no longer introduces any new elset names, so this is moot.

Full suite: 730 passed, 1 pre-existing unrelated failure (ziq). Slow suite:
7 failures, all the same still-open eez bug (unrelated gen3delem issue,
confirmed unchanged by these fixes — verified the exact error signature is
identical before and after).

title: [bug] building_01a fails with CalculiX 'gen3delem: first thickness ... is zero'
description:
Discovered while fixing 51j (overlapping-geometry element loss). After that
fix, portal_01's 4 previously-failing integration tests now pass completely,
but building_01a still fails — CalculiX now gets past the *BEAM SECTION
card-reading stage (51j's bug) and fails later, during STEP 1 processing:

  *ERROR in gen3delem: first thickness
        in node            1  of element           30
        is zero

This is a DIFFERENT, unrelated bug — it was previously hidden because ccx
aborted earlier (during input-deck reading) before ever reaching this later
element-expansion phase. Confirmed pre-existing and independent of 51j's fix.

INVESTIGATION SO FAR (inconclusive — needs fresh eyes or CCX source access):
- Programmatically verified NO missing or zero-value *NODAL THICKNESS entries
  anywhere in the generated analysis.inp (checked every S3 element's 3 nodes
  against the *NODAL THICKNESS block — full coverage, all values > 0, no
  duplicates).
- The literal node/element IDs in ccx's error message ("node 1", "element 30")
  do not appear to be literal global IDs from our file:
  - Global node ID 1 is a beam-only node (used by B31 element 1), and the
    project's meshing design deliberately keeps beam and shell nodes disjoint
    (separate point registries in gmsh_geometry.py, see CLAUDE.md) — it
    should be impossible for a shell element to reference node 1.
  - The 30th S3 element in file order (literal ID 170, nodes [226, 279, 79])
    has a valid thickness entry for node 226 (0.25).
  - The 30th element in total file order across all *ELEMENT blocks (literal
    ID 31, a B31 element) has a valid, non-degenerate *BEAM SECTION
    (RECT 0.45 x 0.45).
  So "node 1 of element 30" in ccx's message likely refers to ccx's own
  internal renumbering/array-index scheme (per-type or per-expansion-pass),
  not literal IDs from our .inp — needs correlating against CalculiX source
  (gen3delem / gen3dshell routines) or a minimal, hand-built repro to pin
  down which physical element/node it actually is.

REPRODUCE:
  python -m ifc_structural_mechanics.cli analyze \
    examples/analysis-models/ifcFiles/building_01a.ifc --output /tmp/b01a
  (fails with return code 201 during STEP 1, after 51j's fix is applied)

  Affects tests/integration/test_results_json.py::TestBuilding01aResultsJson
  (4 tests, marked @pytest.mark.slow).

NEXT STEPS:
- Try a minimal 2-member repro (one shell member overlapping another, similar
  to building_01a's 2RB3iddKX1KOhkwm7i6S3G member) to narrow down whether the
  overlap-fallback for SurfaceMembers has an analogous issue to what 51j fixed
  for CurveMembers/U1.
- Consider instrumenting/building CalculiX from source with debug prints in
  gen3delem to get the real element/node identity, or bisect the .inp file by
  progressively removing shell members until the error disappears.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (2026-07-03), using CalculiX 2.23 source at
~/rpmbuild/BUILD/calculix-ccx-2.23-build/CalculiX/ccx_2.23/src/gen3delem.f:

gen3delem.f's node-count-determination loop (lines 118-144) filters out
C3D/D/G/E/MASS element types before assigning `numnod`, but does NOT
exclude 'U' (user elements, i.e. our TYPE=U1 beams). When the loop
reaches a U1 element, the local Fortran variable `numnod` is simply left
at whatever value a previously-processed B31/S3/etc. element set it to
(none of the if/elseif branches match a U1 element's lakon string, and
Fortran does not reset locals between iterations). The loop then reads
thicke(1,indexe+j) for j=1..numnod. *BEAM SECTION,SECTION=GENERAL (the
card U1 requires) never populates `thicke` at all -- confirmed in
beamgeneralsections.f lines 367-389, guarded by `if(section.ne.'GENE')`.
So this read is always exactly 0, and gen3delem aborts with "first
thickness in node <j> of element <i> is zero" (j and i here are the
LOCAL node index and CCX's internal element number -- NOT global node
IDs, contrary to earlier investigation notes).

Confirmed with minimal repros (saved under /tmp/ccxrepro during
investigation, not committed): a lone U1 element succeeds; adding ANY
other B31 or S3 element anywhere in the same file crashes, REGARDLESS of
element ID ordering (tested U1 first and U1 second -- both crash). So
this is NOT an ordering/numbering bug fixable from the .inp writer side
-- it depends on stack-garbage state left by unrelated parsing code, and
is unavoidable whenever U1 coexists with any other 1D/2D element.

Confirmed against upstream: github.com/Dhondtguido/CalculiX (official
mirror, commit 6d460bc, 2026-06-19) still has the identical unguarded
filter -- bug is NOT fixed upstream as of this writing.

FIX APPLIED (two parts):
1. patches/calculix-gen3delem-user-element.patch -- one-line CalculiX
   source fix (add `.and.(lakon(i)(1:1).ne.'U')` to the filter).
   Verified by patching+rebuilding CCX 2.23 locally: both minimal repros
   and the full building_01a.inp now pass gen3delem cleanly (building_01a
   then hits a separate, already-documented "matrix found to be
   singular" -- the known mechanism-risk limitation, unrelated to this
   bug and out of scope here).
2. CalculixRunner._raise_if_known_gen3delem_user_element_bug()
   (analysis/calculix_runner.py) detects the "gen3delem...thickness"
   signature + mixed U1/native element types in the .inp and raises a
   clear, actionable AnalysisError instead of the generic CCX message,
   pointing at the patch. Unit tests added in
   tests/unit/analysis/test_calculix_runner.py
   (TestGen3delemUserElementBugDetection).
3. Documented in CLAUDE.md Known Limitations.

Not yet done: submitting the patch upstream to Dhondtguido/CalculiX
(GitHub issue -- repo has issues enabled, 67 open, actively used). Patch
file and repro are ready; needs a human-authorized post since it's a
public external action.
close_reason: Root cause confirmed as a CalculiX 2.23 gen3delem.f bug (missing 'U'-prefix exclusion for USER ELEMENT types); fixed via source patch (patches/calculix-gen3delem-user-element.patch, verified by rebuilding CCX) plus a code-side clear-error detection in CalculixRunner

title: Warn when a directional section is analysed in a default (non-IFC) orientation
description:
When the beam normal cannot be taken from the IFC orientation, the writer silently falls back to a CANONICAL perpendicular (global Y->X->Z) — _get_beam_normal geometry fallback (unified_calculix_writer.py:180-229) and the U1 orthogonalise fallback (writer.py:951-960). For symmetric sections (circle, square, pipe) orientation is immaterial, but for DIRECTIONAL sections (rectangle, I, T, C) a wrong orientation interchanges the strong and weak bending axes — a result-affecting limitation that is currently emitted at most as logger.info, and the orthogonalise fallback is fully silent. Nothing reaches result['warnings'].

This is the user-facing counterpart to the orientation bug (ifc_structural_mechanics-c9l). Even after that fix, members with no usable IFC .Axis will still be placed in a default orientation and the user must be told.
design: When a canonical/default orientation is used for a member whose section is directional (non-axisymmetric — i.e. not circle/pipe/square), append a warning to result['warnings'] naming the member id and IFC GlobalId, and emit logger.warning. Determine 'directional' from section_type and, where needed, Iy != Iz. Route via the same warnings channel as the section-approximation warnings. Should NOT warn for axisymmetric sections or for members whose IFC .Axis was honoured. The geometric default now applies only when member.local_axis is None, in _split_beam_sets_by_orientation and _get_beam_normal - those are the two places this warning belongs.

title: Native B31 beam-section path lacks beam-normal orthogonalisation safety net
description:
The U1/GENERAL section writer (_write_beam_section_general, meshing/unified_calculix_writer.py:947) orthogonalises the beam normal against the actual beam axis (computed from element node coords) and falls back to a canonical perpendicular if degenerate. The native B31 path (_write_beam_section_for_set, ~writer.py:743) does NOT do this — it writes whatever _get_beam_normal() returns directly on line 2 of the *BEAM SECTION card. If that vector is parallel/near-parallel to the beam axis (which it currently always is for members with an IFC .Axis — see the related bug), CalculiX gets a degenerate local system.

This is defence-in-depth: even after the _get_beam_normal fix, the native path should guarantee the emitted normal is unit-length and perpendicular to the beam axis.
design: Extract the orthogonalise-and-fallback logic from _write_beam_section_general into a shared helper (e.g. _orthogonal_beam_normal(raw_normal, elem_ids)) that computes the beam axis from the first element's node coords, subtracts the parallel component, and falls back to a canonical perpendicular when degenerate. Call it from BOTH the native B31 path and the U1 path so there is a single source of truth.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Test written FIRST: feed a native RECT member a beam normal parallel to its axis and assert the *BEAM SECTION line-2 vector written is unit-length and perpendicular to the beam axis (not parallel).
2. Orthogonalisation logic is shared between native and U1 paths (no duplication).
3. Existing section tests pass; linters clean.
close_reason: Shared orthogonalise-and-fallback helper (_compute_beam_axis/_orthogonal_beam_normal) extracted from U1 path and applied to native B31 path (_write_beam_section_for_set). Added test_beam_normal_safety_net.py covering parallel-normal correction, no-op on already-perpendicular normals, and vertical-column case. All existing tests + linters pass.

title: Buckling benchmark finds no eigenvalues in .dat file
description:
test_buckling_benchmark.py has two tests. PARTIAL FIX applied:

1. test_buckling_eigenvalue_parsed — NOW PASSES after fix in results_parser.py. CalculiX writes 'B U C K L I N G   F A C T O R   O U T P U T' (spaced letters) but parser checked for 'BUCKLING FACTOR'. Fixed: trigger now matches 'B U C K L I N G' OR 'BUCKLING FACTOR'. Also fixed block termination: was ending on column headers before any data, now only ends after data is collected.

2. test_first_eigenvalue_matches_euler — STILL FAILS. Parsed eigenvalue = 18.71, but Euler analytical P_cr = 1.728e7 N (6 orders of magnitude off). Hypothesis: CalculiX B31 elements are expanded internally to C3D8I solid elements, and the geometric stiffness from this internal representation does not reproduce Euler column buckling accurately at the macro level. The INP uses 10 B31 elements, RECT 0.1x0.1 section, 1N preload along beam axis.

NEXT STEPS: investigate CalculiX B31 buckling behavior — either (a) switch the benchmark to use shell/solid elements (S4R or C3D8) to avoid B31 internal expansion issues, or (b) read CalculiX docs on BUCKLE with B31 to find what eigenvalue it actually produces, or (c) change the test to validate a known-correct CalculiX B31 buckling case.
notes: 2026-10-09 review: this test is one of the three things keeping CI red. Eigenvalue differs by ccx build (18.7 locally on the Copr build, 1.69 on Ubuntu CI), so the value is not just a unit error. Note 8go (validate buckling) was closed while this still fails.
close_reason: Two causes. (1) The benchmark left the column free to spin about its own axis (pins fixed DOF 1-3 only), so the system was singular and the eigenvalue was noise that differed by ccx build. (2) Loads were in a preceding *STATIC step; CalculiX only scales loads defined inside the *BUCKLE step. The library writer had the same two-step form, so linear_buckling returned meaningless factors (1.2e13 for the Euler column, not scaling with load). Writer now emits one *BUCKLE step with the loads; benchmark gives 1.693e7 N vs Euler 1.727e7 N (2.0%, shear-flexible B31).

Keys, units, and structure can change between versions without warning, breaking downstream tools that process the results. title: Support I-section beam profiles natively
description: Only rectangular, circular, pipe (hollow circle), and box (hollow rectangle) cross-sections are supported for CalculiX B31 beam elements. I-sections are currently approximated as equivalent rectangles preserving area and second moment of area. Proper CalculiX B31 I-section support should be added.

title: Support partial connection end-releases
description: Connection end-releases read from IfcRelConnectsStructuralMember.AppliedCondition are modelled as full pins (all three rotational DOFs released). Partial releases — where only one member or one rotation axis is released — are not yet supported.

title: Fix overlapping members losing physical group during mesh fragmentation
description: Members with identical or overlapping geometry may lose their physical group assignment during fragment(). Their sections are skipped with a warning; a fallback assigns the nearest elements by spatial proximity. Need a robust fix so physical groups survive fragmentation.
close_reason: Exact-overlap members now share a combined physical group ('A||B'). Writer parses pipe-separated names and assigns elements to all named members. Partial-overlap fallback preserved.

title: Fix connection geometry: use IFC topology instead of proximity search
description: Currently connections are resolved by geometric proximity (0.5 m tolerance) rather than using the IfcRelConnectsStructuralMember relationship topology defined in the IFC file. This can cause incorrect connectivity for closely spaced but unconnected members.
close_reason: Replaced 0.5m proximity search with endpoint-targeting: uses domain model geometry to find member endpoint closest to connection position, then matches mesh node within 10mm. Falls back to 0.5m for members without geometry.

title: IfcGridPlacement for structural items and actions
description: Split from aiz.58. get_transformation() raises E-IFC-003 for IfcGridPlacement (and for an IfcLocalPlacement whose PlacementRelTo is one). Placement location is an IfcVirtualGridIntersection: two IfcGridAxis curves (in the grid's own ObjectPlacement axes) intersected after OffsetDistances (offset of each axis, third value along z); PlacementRefDirection is an IfcDirection or a second intersection. Check the IFC4.3 spec for the offset side (SameSense) and test against a hand-built file; check whether ifcopenshell.util.placement has a helper now. No example model uses it.

title: Temperature loads (IfcStructuralLoadTemperature)
description: Split from aiz.58. IfcStructuralLoadTemperature on curve/surface actions: DeltaTConstant (uniform) and DeltaTY/DeltaTZ (difference between outer fibres in member local y/z; sign conventions in the IFC spec notes). Needs the material's thermal expansion coefficient (Pset_MaterialThermal.ThermalExpansionCoefficient or IfcMaterialProperties) - raise if missing, never assume. CalculiX: *EXPANSION on the material, *TEMPERATURE per step with *INITIAL CONDITIONS TYPE=TEMPERATURE; beams and shells take gradients on *TEMPERATURE data lines (check manual for 2.21 and 2.23). Equivalent-rectangle and torsion-corrected materials need their own expansion; gradients over an equivalent rectangle's depth differ from the real section's (curvature = alpha*DeltaT/h needs the real depth). Reset per step as loads are. Reactions balance each other (no applied load). Benchmarks: clamped bar under uniform DeltaT (N = EA alpha DeltaT), cantilever under gradient (tip deflection alpha DeltaT L^2/(2h)), fixed-fixed under gradient (M = EI alpha DeltaT/h). Measure CalculiX first.

title: results.json: deflected shapes, surface member fields and buckling mode shapes (settle with Bonsai first)
description:
Split from 94g.11, whose documentation, run record, warnings and limits are done (schema 1.10). What remains enlarges the file, so settle with Bonsai (IfcOpenShell issue 9866) which they want before adding it:

- Deflected shape of curve members: displacements along each member (distance_m plus ux, uy, uz and rotations, per case and combination), like section_force_diagrams.
- Surface members: nodal values on some mesh, or points keyed to the outline, for a contour; plate moments, membrane forces and shear per unit length, which slabs and walls are designed from.
- Buckling mode shapes (only the factors now). They are scaled to a largest value of one, so they are shapes, not displacements.
- For export as IFC structural results (see 94g.11 notes): displacements at connections (IfcStructuralLoadSingleDisplacement), the load groups' GlobalIds for load cases, the section axes of diagrams as vectors, theory type for the result group.
- A JSON Schema in the package validated against docs/examples/beam_01_results.json, if consumers want one; docs/results_schema.md is prose.

title: A support holds every node coincident with it, members it does not hold included
description: Found in aiz.51. find_support_nodes() returns the nearest node and every node coincident with it (beam and shell meshes keep separate nodes at one point), whatever members the connection holds. A support connected only to a beam, at a corner of a slab hinged to that beam along a line connection, clamped the slab's corner node too (DOF 1-6 on a shell node): the hinged slab came out 15% stiff in TestSlabJoinedToBeamsAlongALine until the benchmark moved its supports off the slab. Restrict the coincident nodes to those of the members the connection holds (connected_members), and check what that changes in the example models (a support at a slab corner with no point connection between beam and slab there).

title: U1 member with missing section or material is skipped with a warning

CLAUDE.md principle 6 (aiz.12): never leave an entity out and carry on. Should raise AnalysisError naming the member. Found while doing bgz; not reached by any test (extraction already refuses a member without section/material, so this may be dead, in which case remove the branch).

Since 94g.8 every support that holds a rotation has moments, so the total about the origin (sum of M + position x F over the supports) can be given, with the moment of the applied loads beside it as the check; or the keys should go. Connections 48 (1yxPIFngDFmRsC7POMtP6B) and 49 (1JI4zFzbT2zfFWEKe$8wC_) have four members each, all eccentric, so no member has a node at the connection: _merge_rigid_connection_nodes() takes the nearest end (a beam end 150 mm away) as the joint and links the other three to it. 3 links for 4 ends, twice: 115 for 117. title: Section forces of members tied to a surface along their length go up and down from one cross-section to the next
description: Found with aiz.84 (2026-10-12). building_01 at a 0.5 m mesh: 22 curve members are tied to a wall or slab along their length (_build_line_bearings), 7 overlap another member. In several of them N and V change sign and size from one cross-section to the next (0s3QRbmCb4n9 Dead N: -4622, -1162, +900, -389, -318 kN over 0.85 m; 295S6KgXX8ZO Dead Vf2 between -30 and +33 kN). A tie brings a force in at every beam node, the middle node of each element included, so the middle cross-section is not one-sided and _restore_jumps() has nothing to go by: where no line has more than half of seven cross-sections on it, it now leaves the solver's averaged values. The envelope of such a member (max_N_N, max_Vf*) is then of doubtful meaning and nothing in results.json says so. To do: decide what to report for these members (a warning naming how many, or the forces from equilibrium of the tie forces), and check whether the size of the forces near the ends is real (the file's 202 t/m3 masonry) or a singularity of tying a beam node to one shell triangle.

The zig-zag is not a property of the ties: a beam tied to a slab under its own and the slab's weight has a smooth diagram (TestSlabBearingOnBeams at 0.25 and 0.125 m). It appears where force passes between member and surface at a point (a column in a wall, the end of a wall) and does not converge: 0s3Q Dead N in its first element -3457, -871, +1717 kN at 0.5 m and -4145, -834, +2574 kN at 0.25 m. Nothing is smoothed. results.json now marks members tied along their length with tied_to_surface_members (schema 1.5) and the tie warning says their forces are their share only and mesh dependent where force passes at a point. Not done: forces from the equilibrium of the tie forces (they would be the same unconverged solution, a third smaller at element ends).

title: A point action in LOCAL_COORDS is applied in global axes
description: LoadsExtractor._in_global_axes() leaves a force given in LOCAL_COORDS as it is, for the writer to turn with the member's axes. That happens for line and area loads (coordinate_system = 'local') and, since aiz.58, for the point forces of a DISCRETE curve action. An IfcStructuralPointAction in LOCAL_COORDS gets neither coordinate_system nor member_reference, so its force and moment are applied in global axes with no warning. No example file has one. The local axes of a point action are those of the item it is assigned to: a member's, or a point connection's ConditionCoordinateSystem. Either turn it (connection.local_axes exists in the domain model) or raise.
close_reason: A point action in LOCAL_COORDS is now turned with the axes of the item it is assigned to: a member's local_axis, or a connection's local_axes (ConditionCoordinateSystem of a point connection; global when it has none), as IfcStructuralActivity defines them. LoadsExtractor._point_load() sets coordinate_system and member_reference (the item's GlobalId); _to_global_axes() looks the id up among members, then connections. Assigned to no item or to a surface connection it raises ModelExtractionError. Benchmarks: a rafter rising 3 in 4 and a joint with a turned system give reactions of 0.8 P and 0.6 P (ccx 2.23 and 2.21); two extraction tests on beam_01.

title: Hold members along a skew axis that are free to spin
description: _hold_spinning_members() holds a member nothing stops spinning about its own axis only when the member lies along a global axis (a *BOUNDARY on one rotation DOF at a support). A rafter or a brace on two ball supports is only reported ('could not be held automatically; their displacements include an arbitrary rotation'). title: Plausibility warnings are raised on buckling mode shapes
description: In a linear_buckling analysis the displacement sets in the result file are normalised mode shapes, not displacements. plausibility_warnings() reads them as load cases step_2..step_N and warns that the model deflects by 100 m and is probably a mechanism, twice per mode. Seen on a plane truss in buckling (94g.3 round). Skip the size checks for buckling, or label the modes as modes.

A buckling run without factors is a ResultProcessingError.

title: Straight run of rigidly joined members that can spin is not detected in a space structure
description: _hold_spinning_members() takes a member to be held in torsion when it joins another member without a torsional release. Two collinear members joined rigidly, on supports that hold no rotation about their axis, each count as held by the other and spin together: no hold, no warning. Measured on a 4 m beam of two members on X/Z supports before the plane hold: 8.5 mm deflection for 7.6. Plane structures now find these by kinematics (plane_structure.spinning_members); a space structure still does not. Fix: use the same rigid-body count in 3D, or follow torsion through collinear rigid joints.

Measured: two members on ball supports, 10 kN down and 5 kN across, 12.97/9.15 mm before, 7.638/3.820 now for 7.634/3.817; the same with supports at inner joints. TestStraightRunFreeToSpin, 7 unit tests. Needed aiz.78 for supports at inner joints.

title: Modal analysis: natural frequencies and mode shapes (*FREQUENCY)
description: Asked by Bruno 2026-10-11. CalculiX has a *FREQUENCY step (eigenfrequencies, mode shapes in the FRD, participation factors and effective modal masses in the DAT) and can store the stiffness and mass matrices (keyword to be confirmed against the 2.21 and 2.23 manuals). New analysis type 'modal' following 'Adding a New Analysis Type' in CLAUDE.md: step writing, parsing of frequencies/participation, results.json block, mode shapes for the visualiser. To settle first: mass comes from density only, so loads that are really mass (finishes, imposed) need converting or *MASS elements; equivalent rectangles keep mass per length but not rotary inertia; rigid links and release-hinge arms are massless but very stiff (spurious high modes, conditioning); torsion-corrected rectangles and open sections 30x too stiff in torsion shift torsional modes; members held against spinning. Validate against closed-form beam frequencies (cantilever, simply supported, fixed-fixed) and a plate.

title: Reaction moments where a slab edge is clamped or a member runs on past its support
description: supports[].moments is not_computed there (slab_01, structure_01's wall foot, grid_of_beams whose main beams overhang 0.1 m, 23 of 51 supports in building_02). CalculiX 2.23 writes forces on the expanded nodes of a clamped face to the FRD (*NODE FILE RF): summed about the support they gave force and moment exactly on a clamped bar (-200.0 N m for 200). That would give exact moments for any clamped support, beam or shell, on 2.23 and later; 2.21's are wrong there. For a member running on, the jump in its section forces across the support is the other route.
close_reason: Moments from the solver's forces on the expanded nodes of each support node (*NODE FILE RF), about the support: member ends, clamped slab edges, members running on. results.json schema 1.6, moments: solver. Statics to five figures on a cantilever root, a slab clamped on one edge and a bar clamped along its span; building_02 has moments at all 49 clamped supports (23 had none). Member ends remain the check and the fallback on CalculiX 2.21.

title: Reactions on CalculiX 2.21: total from the supports, and clamped slab edges
description: When the solver's reactions do not balance (CalculiX <= 2.21), global_reactions is still the solver's wrong total, and a support that clamps a slab edge or a member running on past it is marked unreliable with the solver's wrong figures. Possible: give the total as the sum of the supports when every rotation-holding one could be replaced; get the force at a clamped shell edge or an interior beam support from the stresses either side. The member-end fallback also ignores a point load applied exactly at the clamped node.
notes: 2026-10-13 (94g.8): on 2.21 the FRD forces on expanded nodes (*NODE FILE RF) are wrong only at a clamped member end (cantilever_01 root: spurious 11.3 N along the member on one expanded node, moment 25.28 for 27.55); at slab_01's edges, structure_01's wall foot and grid_of_beams' interior supports they equal 2.23's. So a clamped slab edge or an interior beam support is not actually wrong on 2.21: it is marked unreliable only because the step's total does not balance (structure_01: its column foot). Giving the total as the sum of supports after replacing the member-end ones would clear those. Supports' moments now come from these forces (moments: solver) when the step balances and member ends agree.
close_reason: On 2.21 the supports are added up once the member-end ones are replaced: if they balance the loads to 1% the others keep the solver's forces and moments (structure_01's wall foot) and, where the solver's own total does not balance, global_reactions gives the supports' (forces: supports, schema 1.8; portal_01 42 701.0 for 42 702.9 N, solver 38 029). title: Decide: correct the torsional stiffness of solid rectangular beams (CalculiX is up to 18.5% too stiff)
description: Measured 2026-10-11 from the twist of the solver's own nodes (TestTorsion): CalculiX's expanded beam has one solid element across the section, which can only warp as x2*x3, so J = a^3 b^3 / 3(a^2+b^2): 1.185 x Saint-Venant for a square, 1.164 for 1:2, exact for a thin strip. converters/section_profiles.expanded_rectangle_torsion_stiffness() is this formula and matches measurement to three figures. An earlier benchmark compared tip deflection on element faces and the error was hidden by the arm's rotation. Option: write solid rectangles with the orthotropic material too and scale both shear moduli by J_true/J_fe (0.84 for a square), as aiz.50 did for tubes, boxes and bars. Cost: shear stiffness 16% too low for a square (a few percent of deflection on stocky members), every rectangle benchmark shifts, and the 5/6-versus-1.0 shear calibration of orthotropic rectangles would need measuring first. Currently documented as a known error in README and validation report.
close_reason: Option 3 (Bruno, 2026-10-11), after measuring: solid rectangles are written with an orthotropic material of their own (MAT_RT_<member>), depth modulus kept, width modulus lowered by rectangle_shear_moduli() until 4PQ/(P+Q) = G J. Measured J/J_sv 1.000 for square, 1:2, 2:1, 1:4 at both element orders; depth-direction deflection unchanged to 4 figures; width direction follows 5/6 of the lowered modulus (27/45/17% soft). One warning per model. Examples: grid_of_beams 0.3727->0.3732, building_01 Live 0.2857->0.2864 and self-weight 6.66->6.78 mm, building_02 Live 25.6->25.7; others identical; reactions unchanged.

title: Rigid beam-slab line connections and eccentricity on line connections

Needs shared nodes along the line (knots) or a conforming mesh between beam and slab. IfcRelConnectsWithEccentricity on such a connection is not read either.
close_reason: Line connections between a curve and a surface member join them along the whole line (they were a point at the midpoint). Geometry meshes the line into the slab node for node with the beam (transfinite); rigid = merged nodes or rigid links (eccentric), released = DOF 1-3 ties. TestSlabJoinedToBeamsAlongALine: strip between stiff beams clamped -0.46%, hinged -0.14% at 0.25 m, in plane and downstand. Arms/equations on the slab middle surface were tried and rejected (shell normals stay free, 40% soft).

title: Decide: match torsion instead of shear for closed and solid sections analysed as equivalent rectangles
description: Measured (TestTorsion): equivalent rectangle torsional stiffness / true = 31 (I 200x400), 0.47 (tube 300x10), 0.67 (box 200x400x10), 0.83 (round bar). Two shear moduli (G12, G13) cannot match two shear areas and J. For open sections nothing helps without wrecking weak-axis shear. For closed and round sections the moduli could be chosen to match J instead (orthotropic rectangle torsion: C = G12 a b^3/3 [1 - (192/pi^5)(b/a) sqrt(G12/G13) sum tanh(n pi a sqrt(G13/G12) / 2b)/n^5]), at the cost of shear stiffness about 1.2x (bar) to 2.2x (thin tube) too high. Torsion matters in grids and space frames, shear deformation is usually a few percent of deflection, so matching torsion for closed sections is probably the better trade. Also: U1 is no better (I 267x, box 1.63x), another reason to remove it.
close_reason: Agreed by Bruno 2026-10-11 and implemented: TORSION_MATCHED_SECTIONS (circular, hollow circular, hollow rectangular) get both shear moduli scaled so that 4PQ/(P+Q) = G J; torsion measured exact (1.000) for two tubes, two boxes and a bar; shear stiffness too high by 1.11 (bar), 1.40 (box 200x400x10), 1.88 (tube 300x10); cantilever benchmarks moved from 0.2% to 1.2%. Documented in README (limitations), CLAUDE.md (Torsion), validation report (Torsion), section_profiles.py docstrings. Finding: solid rectangles are 18.5% too stiff in torsion (aiz.53).

title: U1 and B31 beams sharing a node are not rotationally coupled (joint acts as a pin)
description: On a CalculiX build that gets past the gen3delem crash (the local Copr build), a U1 element and a B31 element sharing a node transfer no moment. Test: 2 m beam along x, fixed at x=0, pinned at x=2, 1000 N at midspan, 0.1x0.1 section, first half B31. Second half B31: midspan deflection 4.05e-5 m (fixed-pinned beam, 4.17e-5 by Euler). Second half U1 with the same A and I: 1.88e-4 m, which is the cantilever-plus-pinned-link answer (1.905e-4). CalculiX expands B31 into bricks and ties their rotation through a knot; the U1 node's own rotational DOFs are not part of that knot. So in any mixed model every U1-to-B31 joint is a hinge: results are wrong without warning, and frames can become mechanisms. building_01 (5 U1 sets plus B31 and S3) fails in spooles factorisation, which this probably explains better than the documented 'pinned column bases' story. This holds even with the gen3delem patch, so the patch alone does not make mixed models usable. Reinforces 31a (equivalent RECT on B31). Until then the writer should refuse or warn loudly when a U1 member shares a node with a B31 member.
acceptance_criteria: Either mixed U1+B31 joints transfer moment (regression test on the model above), or the writer raises/warns for such joints and the docs say so.

title: Recover section forces for U1 (SECTION=GENERAL) members in Python
description:
U1 + SECTION=GENERAL members currently produce no section forces: SF output is
skipped for them (U1 has no SF or stress output in CalculiX), so they have no
section-force or utilisation results.

Work:
- Recover N, V2, V3, T, M2, M3 per U1 element in Python from nodal displacements
  and rotations, using the Timoshenko element stiffness with the same A, I11,
  I22 and shear factor that were written to the INP, minus the fixed-end forces
  of the work-equivalent nodal loads already applied for distributed loads and
  self-weight. meshing/user_element_beam.py is a starting point (it is
  Euler-Bernoulli; U1 is Timoshenko).
- Feed the result into the existing section-force/utilisation export so U1
  members report in the same shape as B31 members.
- Validate against analytical cases (cantilever and simply supported beam, point
  and distributed load).

Scope limit on stock CalculiX (decision 2026-10-09 to stay on stock): U1 crashes
when mixed with any other 1D/2D element (gen3delem bug,
ifc_structural_mechanics-eez), so this only benefits models where every 1D/2D
element is U1, or users running a patched build. Mixed models are covered by the
equivalent-RECT bead. The two paths coexist: U1 gives correct torsional
stiffness (independent J) where it can be used.
acceptance_criteria: An all-U1 model reports section forces and utilisation in the results JSON matching analytical values; black, isort, flake8 and ruff pass.
notes:
2026-10-10: U1 is opt-in now (--open-sections user-element). Default members get section forces from expanded-element stresses (aiz.13). This bead only matters if U1 is kept.
2026-10-14 (aiz.19): analysis/user_element_forces.py has CalculiX's own U1 matrix (e_c3d_u1.f; not the textbook Timoshenko beam, shear terms differ, converges to it) and u1_element_forces(): K_e u_e per element in global axes, from the FRD's six-component DISP. Local end forces from it are the section forces (first end negated). Do not use CalculiX's *EL PRINT S for U1: resultsmech_u1.f recovers with 1/(1-phi) shape functions and gave 728 N shear for 1500. The fix may involve upgrading shared beam+shell node connections to DOF 1-6 EQUATION constraints where appropriate.

title: Knots at clamped supports stiffen bending over one element length
description: Found while fixing aiz.76. A knot (rigid cross-section) stops the expanded section distorting as bending makes it, which stiffens a member over the elements next to it. Measured: 4 m beam, 10 kN at midspan on a knot: -3.1% at 0.5 m mesh, -1.7% at 0.25, -0.84% at 0.1, -0.56% at 0.05. A 3 m cantilever (0.1 m square, clamped root, which CalculiX makes a knot) under a tip load is -1.9% at 0.5 m and -0.39% at 0.1 m, with or without a knot at the tip. Joints of members at an angle are knots too. Find out whether this matters at the mesh sizes the example models use (building_02 runs at 2 m) and whether results should say so.
close_reason: Cause was Poisson's ratio of beams: a knot stops the expanded section contracting. Beam materials now written with nu=0 (_BEAM_POISSON); cantilever -0.29% at 0.5/0.25/0.1 m (was -1.2/-0.75/-0.5%). Point loads now knotted at every beam node (not only free ends): I-section fixed-fixed point load exact to 3e-6 at any mesh (was +1.2..3.1% dent).

title: Section forces at element ends are off by w h^2/12 under a load along the element
description: Measured 2026-10-13 (94g.8): the moment integrated from stresses at the end of an element differs from the nodal-force moment there by w h^2/12 (beam_01: 46.1, 11.5, 1.9 N m at 0.5, 0.25, 0.1 m; cantilever_01 root 0.1% low at 0.25 m). It is the linear stress of a reduced-integration quadratic element taken to its ends where the moment is a parabola: the same shift, with the same sign, at every element end, so root and midspan of a fixed beam are both shifted and still satisfy statics between them. The diagrams and envelopes carry it (well inside the 1% they are documented to). The support moments no longer do. Possible: correct the diagram with the load known on each element, or take end values from the element middles and the shear. Nothing is assumed of the load today (aiz.84), so think before adding that.
close_reason: ResultsExporter._correct_curvature(): after the shear jumps are restored, each element's moments are corrected by its own change of shear times its length (ends +dV h/12, middle -dV h/24; one value at shared cross-sections, by the mean of the two errors). _member_records() caches the corrected copies; diagrams, envelope, max_normal_stress_Pa and _member_ends_at (moment vectors too) read them. beam_01 diagram end vs solver support moment: 46.1/11.5/1.9 -> 0.12/0.06/0.11 N m at 0.5/0.25/0.1 m; cantilever_01 diagram vs w(L-x)^2/2 at 0.5 m: 0.128 -> 0.0002 N m. Fast suite, slow suite (19) and validation+integration on 2.21 pass.

title: Poisson's ratio assumed 0.3 when the file gives a shear modulus
description: portal_01's ASTM A36 has YoungModulus 29e6 and ShearModulus 11.2e6 psi in Pset_MaterialMechanical and no PoissonRatio. MembersExtractor warns and assumes 0.3, where E / 2G - 1 = 0.2946 is in the file. Use the shear modulus when it is given; the effect on portal_01 is 0.4% in shear stiffness. Re-measure the portal_01 figures in docs/validation_report.md and README.md after.

The by-name second pass reads ShearModulus too (beam_01 and building_0x keep theirs in a pset named after the material; all consistent). portal_01: nu 0.2946, reactions moved under 0.01% (thrust 6206.0 -> 6205.5 N at 0.25 m); plane-frame reference recomputed with the file's G: 1386.37 lbf; docs re-measured.

title: Plane-structure check ignores joints made by the mesh
description: Found in aiz.80. fragment() gives curve members that touch one mesh node (a member ending on the span of another, two that cross), which is a rigid joint, whether or not a connection of the file joins them. building_02 has 334 such places (263 beam on beam, 71 column ending on a beam, all end-on at right angles; each such end has a connection of its own that joins nothing else), building_01 has 2. Since aiz.80 one warning counts them and the spin check treats them as joints. Not decided: (1) is rigid the right reading? A beam lying in a slab with no connection is tied in translation only (a hinge line); a pin here would be consistent with that and would take the torsion out of building_02's girders, and change its results. (2) --strict-connections promises only the connections in the file, but leaves these joints in; taking them apart needs the shared node split, and building_02's secondary beams would then hang on their slab ties alone. (3) analysis/plane_structure.py (out_of_plane_freedoms, spinning_members) still reasons from the file's connections alone, so a plane frame joined this way may be held where it need not be. Needs Bruno's ruling on (1) and (2) before code. Measured for a small grid in TestBeamEndingOnTheSpanOfAnother (docs/validation_report.md).
notes: Ruling 2026-10-12 (Bruno): members that align with no explicit connection get a rigid, full moment connection, as analysis software does. IFC4.3 specification read the same day (IfcRelConnectsStructuralMember, IfcStructuralItem, IfcStructuralCurveMember, IfcStructuralConnection): members are joined through connection objects alone, 'point connections at each end of the member', topology 'meant to share vertices and edges'; nothing on members that only touch, and no default. So questions (1) and (2) are settled: rigid, and strict connections leaves them joined. What remains is (3): analysis/plane_structure.py (out_of_plane_freedoms, spinning_members) reasons from the file's connections alone.

title: Spinning members in a space structure: check that the member across can hold
description: After aiz.72 a member or straight run counts as held in torsion by any member across it that it joins without a torsional release. Whether that member can itself give way is not checked: a beam and a column in an L with ball supports only at the beam's far end and at the joint turn together about the beam's axis and nothing is said (tests/unit/meshing/test_spinning_members.py::test_member_joined_to_another_is_taken_as_held is that model). The plane case is done by a rigid-body count (analysis/plane_structure.py); the same count in three dimensions would find these, but it must know every tie the mesh makes (nodes shared after fragment() without a connection of the file, line bearings, surfaces), or it will hold members that need no help and so add a restraint that carries moment.

title: Recognise plane structures in a skew plane or with surface members
description: plane_normal() only accepts curve members in a plane parallel to two global axes. A frame drawn in a vertical plane at an angle in plan, or a plane frame with a shear wall (surface member in the plane), gets no out-of-plane hold. The first needs restraints in skew axes (*TRANSFORM or equations; see aiz.35 skew supports); the second needs the wall's nodes held and its drilling/out-of-plane bending considered. Also still open from 94g.3: run a truss and a frame authored in Bonsai itself.

title: Maybe later: solver-neutral analysis model between the domain model and the writers, then a PyNite backend
description: Only if a second backend goes ahead. What the IFC means at joints lives in UnifiedCalculixWriter (3,080 lines) mixed with CalculiX workarounds. Neutral decisions to extract: eccentric member ends and rigid end zones, joints along a span, implied beam-slab bearing and column-slab ties (and --strict-connections), which rotations a release frees and in which axes, supports in their own axes, work-equivalent nodal loads, the spinning-member hold. CalculiX-only: shared nodes as the only rigid joint, release hinges built from arms, equation term limits, equivalent rectangles and torsion moduli. Without this layer two backends would read the same file differently and a cross-check would measure the readings, not the solvers. Then PyNite for models of curve members only (sections as A, Iy, Iz, J; first independent reference for portal_01). PyNite's limits (plates, no buckling, speed) are untested here. Depends on the exporter split.

description: Only if a second backend (PyNite) goes ahead. ResultsExporter attributes results through CalculiX's expanded solid nodes (FRD element block) and integrates section forces from stresses. A frame solver returns member forces and nodal displacements directly.
